Symfony Consoleを使ったdecisions-lintを作ります。
これはJevやOpenAI Decisions APIを使ったLinterツールです。API Providerの具象クラスとLinter内で扱えるDecision Interface、API ProviderをInterfaceに当てはめるAdapterは必須です。
その上でdecisions.yamlでLinterの設定を書けるようにしてください。RuleはRule用のYamlを定義してdecisions.yamlでimport、設定値の上書きをできるようにします。設定ファイル、ルールファイルにはスキーマ定義してスキーマ検証できるようにしてください。
ルールは非決定的なLintに使います。例えばAnalyzerでanalyzeという公開メソッドを持つのは妥当だよね。じゃあfooというメソッドは？それはAnalyzerが所有するものじゃないよね。みたいなニュアンスの強いものを扱います。また他のケースだとDDDでUseCaseをLintしてドメイン知識が漏れているかなど既存のPHPStanなどのように決定的に検査できない、ニュアンスを扱います。
またReporterを定義していくつかのフォーマットで出力可能にしてください。また違反している行、列などLinterとして必要なものは定義可能でなければいけません。またルール違反は違反しているではなく、違反しているからどう直さないといけないのかをルールとして定義できるようしなければなりません。

https://zenn.dev/kinzal/articles/4bea9e68156889 以前にも似たようなものは作っており、参考にしてください。今回JEVなどが来たことによってより高速で扱いやすいものになる認識です。ただ以前のルール定義が良いとは思っていないのでそこは最適化してください。

コード品質に関してはこのプロジェクトの規約に従ってください。

修正はmainで行い、完了したらコミットください。

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

- buddy: buddyctl CLI: observe the desktop, start/stop Buddy sessions, run session tools (pointer, keyboard, gestures, attention). For long-running Observe watching, also use buddy-observe.
- clickhouse-ingest: Insert data into ClickHouse data warehouse: HTTP/native INSERT, bulk loading, agent session logs, app events. NOT for schema changes (use clickhouse-ops) or querying (use clickhouse-query).
- clickhouse-ops: ClickHouse data warehouse on GPU server (192.168.10.4): Docker Compose, schema DDL, migrations, user admin, retention/TTL, server config. NOT for writing data (use clickhouse-ingest) or querying (use clickhouse-query).
- clickhouse-query: Query and analyze ClickHouse data warehouse: SELECT patterns, agent session analysis, app event analytics, materialized views, system introspection. NOT for schema changes (use clickhouse-ops) or data insertion (use clickhouse-ingest).
- comfyui: ComfyUI on GPU server (192.168.10.4): image generation, inpainting, LoRA, checkpoints, custom nodes, workflow execution, diffusion workflows, data generation pipelines.
- find-docs: Retrieves up-to-date documentation, API references, and code examples for any developer technology. Use this skill whenever the user asks about a specific library, framework, SDK, CLI tool, or cloud service — even for well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. Your training data may not reflect recent API changes or version updates. Always use for: API syntax questions, configuration options, version migration issues, "how do I" questions mentioning a library name, debugging that involves library-specific behavior, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — do not rely on training data for API details, signatures, or configuration options as they are frequently outdated. Always verify against current docs. Prefer this over web search for library documentation and API details.
- gal-advice: Use when the agent wants advice or a blunt second opinion. Run the gal command to get an outside perspective on the situation.
- gpu-containers: Docker containers on GPU server (gpu.internal / 192.168.10.4): NVIDIA GPU workloads, Docker Compose, Caddy LAN reverse proxy, container management, service orchestration, image builds, CUDA deployment. When exposing a new HTTP service, also update proxy/Caddyfile.
- iter: iter CLI: run, compose up, ps, logs, stop, kill, rm, inspect, validate. Foreground/detached runners, ULID/name resolution. Entry point before authoring Iterfile or compose.iter.
- iter-compose: Author or modify compose.iter — iter's multi-service orchestration. Streams, services (build/inline), triggers (cron/watch/files/command/webhook). Stream binding, process model, standalone trigger binaries.
- iter-iterfile: Author or modify an Iterfile (single-service HCL config for iter run). Blocks: workspace, agent, runner, prompt, stream, on-event. Workspace kinds, agent CLI kinds, wait/loop behaviors, conditional expressions.
- localai: LocalAI on GPU server (192.168.10.4): OpenAI-compatible LLM API, model gallery/HuggingFace/Ollama-registry installs, on-demand GPU load/unload, chat, embeddings, vision.
- ollama: Ollama on GPU server (192.168.10.4): LLM inference, chat, vision (LLaVA), embeddings, structured JSON output, tool calling, model management, SD prompt writing via LLM.
- otel-collector-ops: Operate/configure OTel Collector and LGTM deployments: receivers, processors, exporters, pipelines, health checks, signal routing. Debug dropped telemetry after it leaves the app. NOT for app SDK code or querying.
- otel-instrumentation: Add/fix OpenTelemetry instrumentation in application code: OTLP exporters, context propagation, resource attributes, spans, metrics, logs. Debug missing telemetry before it reaches the Collector. NOT for Collector config or querying.
- otel-observe-api: Observe/query existing telemetry via Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo APIs. PromQL, LogQL, trace search/fetch, stack health, datasources. NOT for adding instrumentation (use otel-instrumentation) or Collector config (use otel-collector-ops).

- syncer: Configure and operate the syncer file synchronization CLI: author layered Syncer rules, preserve personal settings with field patches, install native extensions, preview/apply changes, share policies through local/HTTP/Git sources, and troubleshoot compliance. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". # AGENTS

## Vision

Provide tools for AI-assisted PHP development that detect code, test, and configuration problems early and explain how to fix them. This repository is a monorepo of five Composer packages, each with its own dependencies and checks.

## Supported Versions

- **PHP**: 8.0 or later
- **PHPStan**: 1.12 or later on 1.x, and 2.x
- **PHPUnit**: 9.6, 10.5 or later on 10.x, and 11, 12, and 13
- **Rector**: 2.6.7 or later on 2.x, which requires PHPStan 2

## Branching Strategy

This project is developed on `main` only. Commit directly to `main`, whatever the size of the change.

- Do not create branches. A branch cannot be merged back here, so work left on one is stranded.
- Do not open pull requests. They are not part of this project's workflow.
- The common agent habit of branching before committing on a default branch does not apply here: `main` is the working branch.

## Rule Design Principles

- AI-friendly error messages: Every error message must clearly state *what is wrong* and *how to fix it*. An AI agent reading the message should be able to resolve the violation without additional context.
- Specific and identifiable: Messages must include enough detail (e.g., the offending symbol name, the expected pattern) so that each violation can be individually targeted in `ignoreErrors` configurations. Vague messages like "invalid code" are not acceptable.

## Documents

- [DocGen](packages/docgen-php/docs/docgen.md): How the DocGen CLI builds a static HTML documentation site from Composer package source and PHPDoc, with no configuration file of its own.
- [DocGen architecture](packages/docgen-php/docs/architecture.md): How a DocGen run is split into discovery, parsing, analysis, comparison, and rendering, and which layer may depend on which.
- [Guard policies](packages/guard-php/docs/policies.md): What Guard checks against `guard.yaml`, which findings fail the command, and which configuration values it can repair.
- [Guard command line](packages/guard-php/docs/cli.md): How to list the effective rules, check a project, record a baseline, repair configuration, and create the first `guard.yaml`.
- [Guard configuration](packages/guard-php/docs/configuration.md): How `guard.yaml` combines imported presets with project overrides, and which files a run is allowed to read.
- [Guard metrics](packages/guard-php/docs/metrics.md): How to cap the length and cyclomatic complexity of production PHP, and how to give some paths a different profile.
- [Guard structure](packages/guard-php/docs/structure.md): How to restrict the files and subdirectories each directory may contain, including their names and how many are allowed.
- [Guard documents](packages/guard-php/docs/documents.md): How to require a Markdown file to follow a declared outline, badge list, or exact text, and how undeclared files are reported.
- [Guard configuration fields](packages/guard-php/docs/fields.md): How to require a specific value in another tool's configuration file, and when `guard fix` can write that value.
- [Guard extensions](packages/guard-php/docs/extensions.md): How to add a custom check, and a parser for the files that check reads, to the same run as the built-in policies.
- [PHPStan rules](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/phpstan.md): The toolkit PHPStan rules for patterns common in AI-written PHP, with each rule's identifier and how to turn it on or off.
- [PHPStan AI Formatter](packages/phpstan-ai-formatter/README.md): How to install the formatter that prints PHPStan findings for a coding agent, and what that output contains.
- [PHPUnit AI Reporter and Doctest](packages/phpunit-ai-reporter/README.md): How to install the reporter that prints PHPUnit failures for a coding agent, and how Doctest runs PHPDoc examples as tests.

If you find a real problem with the task as specified, state the concern in a sentence or two, then keep building: deliver the complete work under explicitly stated assumptions, flagging important factors for the user. Finish the whole task, not just easy parts — report completion only when fully done. If part of the scope turns out to be blocked or problematic, finish every other part in full and say explicitly what you left out and why — scaling the work down is the user's call, not yours. Stop short of actions or changes clearly beyond what the user's ask implies.

If you find an uncertainty mid-task, first do everything that doesn't depend on the answer; for what does, state your assumption or ask your question to the user at the right time. Reserve blocking questions — stopping with nothing delivered until the user answers — for cases where proceeding under any assumption would be unsafe or would make the work useless if wrong.

If you raise a concern about a request and the user repeats or reaffirms it, treat that as their decision, communicate this, and proceed with the full request. Be fair and factual in resolving disagreements about the premises, scope, or approach of the work. Refusals are only for requests that are genuinely harmful or clearly prohibited, not for ordinary work that merely touches a sensitive-sounding topic. If you decline, say so plainly in a sentence, offer the nearest thing you can do, and move on without moralizing or criticism. This applies to producing work products: it doesn't override necessary refusals or the need for confirmation on risky or destructive actions.

# Writing for the user
The user may not see your tool calls, tool results, or the text you write between them. Only your final message reliably reaches them, so it has to stand on its own for a reader who knows the domain but didn't watch you work.

Rules for that message:
- Lead with the answer or outcome. If something could not be verified, say so first. Keep it short by leaving things out, not by packing them in.
- One idea per sentence, about 20 words, with a verb. Short does not mean clipped: a sentence beats a label with a colon. Start a new sentence instead of joining clauses with a semicolon.
- No em-dashes, no parentheticals, no arrows.
- State facts and conclusions. Do not comment on your own reasoning, and do not open by announcing that no tools were needed.
- Do not refer to anything by a name you made up during the session. Expand uncommon acronyms the first time you use them. Say who wrote a message and what it said, not by number or label.
- Keep code out of prose. Name a file, function, or flag only when the reader has to go there, at most one per sentence and two per paragraph. Describe the rest in words. Commands, snippets, and error text go in a fenced code block.
- Keep numbers out of prose. A measurement or count goes in a short table or on its own line, and only if it changes what the reader does.
- Use a bulleted or numbered list for parallel items: findings, steps, options, files to look at. One or two sentences per bullet, never a paragraph. Bold the first few words of a bullet or paragraph, never a whole sentence. A single point or a line of argument stays in prose.
- No headers in a message under about 500 words. Above that, at most three. If the user asks for no formatting, use none.
- Stop when the content stops. No closing offer, no restating what you did.

You are operating autonomously. The user is not watching in real time and cannot answer questions mid-task, so asking 'Want me to…?' or 'Shall I…?' will block the work. For reversible actions that follow from the original request, proceed without asking. Stop only for destructive actions or genuine scope changes the user must decide. Offering follow-ups after the task is done is fine; asking permission before doing the work is not.

Exception: when the user is describing a problem, asking a question, or thinking out loud rather than requesting a change, the deliverable is your assessment. Report your findings and stop. Don't apply a fix until they ask for one.

Before ending your turn, check your last paragraph. If it is a plan, an analysis, a question, a list of next steps, or a promise about work you have not done ('I'll…', 'let me know when…'), do that work now with tool calls. That includes retrying after errors and gathering missing information yourself. Do not stop because the context or session is long. End your turn only when the task is complete or you are blocked on input only the user can provide.

Before running a command that changes system state (such as restarts, deletes, or config edits), check that the evidence actually supports that specific action. A signal that pattern-matches to a known failure may have a different cause.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:

- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

Contents of /Users/ab/Projects/php-ai-toolkit/AGENTS.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):

# AGENTS

## Vision

Provide tools for AI-assisted PHP development that detect code, test, and configuration problems early and explain how to fix them. This repository is a monorepo of five Composer packages, each with its own dependencies and checks.

## Supported Versions

- **PHP**: 8.0 or later
- **PHPStan**: 1.12 or later on 1.x, and 2.x
- **PHPUnit**: 9.6, 10.5 or later on 10.x, and 11, 12, and 13
- **Rector**: 2.6.7 or later on 2.x, which requires PHPStan 2

## Branching Strategy

This project is developed on `main` only. Commit directly to `main`, whatever the size of the change.

- Do not create branches. A branch cannot be merged back here, so work left on one is stranded.
- Do not open pull requests. They are not part of this project's workflow.
- The common agent habit of branching before committing on a default branch does not apply here: `main` is the working branch.

## Rule Design Principles

- AI-friendly error messages: Every error message must clearly state *what is wrong* and *how to fix it*. An AI agent reading the message should be able to resolve the violation without additional context.
- Specific and identifiable: Messages must include enough detail (e.g., the offending symbol name, the expected pattern) so that each violation can be individually targeted in `ignoreErrors` configurations. Vague messages like "invalid code" are not acceptable.

## Documents

- [DocGen](packages/docgen-php/docs/docgen.md): How the DocGen CLI builds a static HTML documentation site from Composer package source and PHPDoc, with no configuration file of its own.
- [DocGen architecture](packages/docgen-php/docs/architecture.md): How a DocGen run is split into discovery, parsing, analysis, comparison, and rendering, and which layer may depend on which.
- [Guard policies](packages/guard-php/docs/policies.md): What Guard checks against `guard.yaml`, which findings fail the command, and which configuration values it can repair.
- [Guard command line](packages/guard-php/docs/cli.md): How to list the effective rules, check a project, record a baseline, repair configuration, and create the first `guard.yaml`.
- [Guard configuration](packages/guard-php/docs/configuration.md): How `guard.yaml` combines imported presets with project overrides, and which files a run is allowed to read.
- [Guard metrics](packages/guard-php/docs/metrics.md): How to cap the length and cyclomatic complexity of production PHP, and how to give some paths a different profile.
- [Guard structure](packages/guard-php/docs/structure.md): How to restrict the files and subdirectories each directory may contain, including their names and how many are allowed.
- [Guard documents](packages/guard-php/docs/documents.md): How to require a Markdown file to follow a declared outline, badge list, or exact text, and how undeclared files are reported.
- [Guard configuration fields](packages/guard-php/docs/fields.md): How to require a specific value in another tool's configuration file, and when `guard fix` can write that value.
- [Guard extensions](packages/guard-php/docs/extensions.md): How to add a custom check, and a parser for the files that check reads, to the same run as the built-in policies.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

Tools for AI-assisted PHP development: project policy checks, PHPStan rules,
readable analysis and test reports, executable PHPDoc examples, and API documentation.

## Packages

Each package has its own Composer manifest, configuration, and tests. Follow its
README for requirements, installation, usage, and available agent skills.

CI publishes each package to `https://github.com/k-kinzal/<package>` for
Packagist. See [publishing and release instructions](docs/publishing.md) for
the synchronization workflow, repository credentials, and submission steps.

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [guard-php](packages/guard-php/README.md) | Check and repair source, structure, documentation, and configuration policies. |
| [docgen-php](packages/docgen-php/README.md) | Generate PHP API documentation and coverage sites. |
| [phpstan-guard-rules](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/README.md) | Detect PHP and test patterns that need stricter analysis. |
| [doctest-php](packages/doctest-php/README.md) | Run PHPDoc examples as PHPUnit tests. |
| [phpunit-ai-reporter](packages/phpunit-ai-reporter/README.md) | Report test failures for agents and humans. |
| [phpstan-ai-formatter](packages/phpstan-ai-formatter/README.md) | Format PHPStan diagnostics for agents and humans. |

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

$finder = (new PhpCsFixer\Finder())
    ->in(__DIR__)
    ->exclude('build')
    ->exclude('node_modules')
    ->notPath('tests/run.php')
    ->exclude('var')
    ->exclude('vendor');

return (new PhpCsFixer\Config())
    ->setRiskyAllowed(true)
    ->setRules([
        '@PSR12' => true,
        'declare_strict_types' => true,
        'strict_param' => true,
        'strict_comparison' => true,
        'array_syntax' => ['syntax' => 'short'],
        'no_unused_imports' => true,
        'ordered_imports' => ['sort_algorithm' => 'alpha'],
        'single_quote' => true,
        'trailing_comma_in_multiline' => true,
        'no_empty_statement' => true,
        'no_superfluous_elseif' => true,
        'no_useless_else' => true,
        'void_return' => true,
        'no_alias_functions' => true,
        'no_mixed_echo_print' => ['use' => 'echo'],

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<ruleset name="guard-php">
    <description>Checks compatibility with the declared PHP support range.</description>
    <file>src</file>
    <file>tests</file>
    <config name="testVersion" value="8.0-"/>
    <rule ref="PHPCompatibility"/>
</ruleset>

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Composer\InstalledVersions;

$packageRoot = dirname(__DIR__);
$autoloadPath = $packageRoot . '/vendor/autoload.php';

if (!is_file($autoloadPath)) {
    fwrite(STDERR, 'Composer dependencies are missing. Run "composer install" in this package first.' . PHP_EOL);
    exit(1);
}

require $autoloadPath;

if (!InstalledVersions::isInstalled('phpunit/phpunit')) {
    fwrite(STDERR, 'PHPUnit is not installed. Require phpunit/phpunit before running tests.' . PHP_EOL);
    exit(1);
}

$phpUnitVersion = InstalledVersions::getVersion('phpunit/phpunit');

if ($phpUnitVersion === null) {
    fwrite(STDERR, 'The installed phpunit/phpunit package does not expose a version. Install a tagged release.' . PHP_EOL);
    exit(1);
}

$phpUnitMajor = explode('.', $phpUnitVersion)[0];
$configurations = [
    '9' => 'phpunit9.xml.dist',
    '10' => 'phpunit10.xml.dist',
    '11' => 'phpunit11.xml.dist',
    '12' => 'phpunit12.xml.dist',
    '13' => 'phpunit.xml.dist',
];
$configuration = $configurations[$phpUnitMajor] ?? null;

if ($configuration === null) {
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf(
        'Installed PHPUnit major %s is unsupported. Add its configuration to the test runner map.',
        $phpUnitMajor,
    ) . PHP_EOL);
    exit(1);
}

$configurationPath = $packageRoot . '/' . $configuration;

if (!is_file($configurationPath)) {
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf(
        'PHPUnit %s requires %s next to this package\'s composer.json.',
        $phpUnitMajor,
        $configuration,
    ) . PHP_EOL);
    exit(1);
}

$rawArguments = $_SERVER['argv'] ?? null;

if (!is_array($rawArguments)) {
    fwrite(STDERR, 'CLI arguments are unavailable. Run tests/run.php from the command line.' . PHP_EOL);
    exit(1);
}

$arguments = [];

foreach (array_slice($rawArguments, 1) as $argument) {
    if (!is_string($argument)) {
        fwrite(STDERR, 'A CLI argument is invalid. Pass only string arguments to tests/run.php.' . PHP_EOL);
        exit(1);
    }

    $arguments[] = $argument;
}

$parallel = ($arguments[0] ?? null) === '--parallel';

if ($parallel) {
    array_shift($arguments);
}

$runner = $packageRoot . '/vendor/bin/' . ($parallel ? 'paratest' : 'phpunit');

if (!is_file($runner)) {
    fwrite(STDERR, sprintf(
        '%s is not installed. Require the matching development dependency first.',
        $parallel ? 'ParaTest' : 'PHPUnit',
    ) . PHP_EOL);
    exit(1);
}

$memoryLimit = ini_get('memory_limit');

if ($parallel) {
    array_unshift($arguments, '--passthru-php=-d memory_limit=' . $memoryLimit);
}

$command = array_map(
    static fn (string $argument): string => escapeshellarg($argument),
    [
        PHP_BINARY,
        '-d',
        'memory_limit=' . $memoryLimit,
        $runner,
        '--configuration',
        $configurationPath,
        ...$arguments,
    ],
);

passthru(implode(' ', $command), $exitCode);
exit($exitCode);

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'

jobs:
  tests:
    name: Tests (${{ matrix.package }}, PHP ${{ matrix.php }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/${{ matrix.package }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package:
          - docgen-php
          - doctest-php
          - guard-php
          - phpstan-ai-formatter
          - phpstan-guard-rules
          - phpunit-ai-reporter
        php:
          - '8.0'
          - '8.1'
          - '8.2'
          - '8.3'
          - '8.4'
          - '8.5'
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: ${{ matrix.php }}
          extensions: mbstring, pcntl, gd, dom
          coverage: none

      - name: Select the matching lock file
        if: matrix.php != '8.5'
        run: cp "composer.lock.php-${{ matrix.php }}" composer.lock

      - name: Validate the Composer manifest against its lock file
        run: composer validate --strict --no-check-publish

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: composer install --no-interaction --prefer-dist

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Run the tests
        run: composer test

  lint:
    name: Lint (${{ matrix.package }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/${{ matrix.package }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package:
          - docgen-php
          - doctest-php
          - guard-php
          - phpstan-ai-formatter
          - phpstan-guard-rules
          - phpunit-ai-reporter
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: mbstring, gd, dom
          coverage: none

      - name: Validate the Composer manifest against its lock file
        run: composer validate --strict --no-check-publish

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: composer install --no-interaction --prefer-dist

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Check the formatting
        run: composer format:check

      - name: Analyse with PHPStan
        run: composer phpstan

      - name: Check PHP compatibility
        run: composer compat

      - name: Check package guard policies
        run: composer guard

      - name: Check repository guard policies
        if: matrix.package == 'guard-php'
        working-directory: .
        run: php packages/guard-php/bin/guard check --config=guard.yaml

      - name: Check the architecture layers
        run: composer deptrac

141	              .write();

name: Split Monorepo

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '.github/scripts/*-package.sh'
      - '.github/scripts/test-split.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/split.yml'
      - 'packages/**'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

# Main and tag runs share a queue. A release never changes a mirror's main.
concurrency:
  group: split-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || 'publish' }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'

jobs:
  validate:
    name: Check distribution on PHP ${{ matrix.php }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        php: ['8.0', '8.5']
    steps:
      - name: Check out the source
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: ${{ matrix.php }}
          extensions: mbstring, dom
          coverage: none

      - name: Validate and install the distributions; test synchronization
        run: bash .github/scripts/test-split.sh

  split:
    name: Publish ${{ matrix.package }}
    needs: validate
    if: >-
      github.repository == 'k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit' &&
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' &&
      (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package:
          - docgen-php
          - doctest-php
          - guard-php
          - phpstan-ai-formatter
          - phpstan-guard-rules
          - phpunit-ai-reporter
    steps:
      - name: Check out the source
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          coverage: none

      - name: Prepare the package
        id: package
        env:
          PACKAGE: ${{ matrix.package }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Validate and publish the same revision. Skip stale main runs, including
          # manual reruns, instead of overwriting a newer mirror snapshot.
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != tag ]; then
            latest="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)"
            if [ "$latest" != "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ]; then
              echo 'A newer main commit exists; its workflow will publish it.'
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          tag=''
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" = tag ]; then
            tag="$GITHUB_REF_NAME"
          fi
          bash .github/scripts/prepare-package.sh "$PACKAGE" "$RUNNER_TEMP/package" "$tag"
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "secret=SPLIT_$(printf '%s' "$PACKAGE" | tr '[:lower:]-' '[:upper:]_')_SSH_KEY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo 'publish=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Check out the mirror with its deploy key
        if: steps.package.outputs.publish == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          repository: k-kinzal/${{ matrix.package }}
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0
          path: .split-repository
          ssh-key: ${{ secrets[steps.package.outputs.secret] }}

      - name: Push the package snapshot
        if: steps.package.outputs.publish == 'true'
        env:
          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ steps.package.outputs.sha }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.package.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash .github/scripts/push-package.sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/package" .split-repository "$SOURCE_SHA" "$RELEASE_TAG"

name: Docs

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'
  DOCS_BRANCH: gh-pages

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Generate and publish the documentation site
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: mbstring, pcntl, gd
          coverage: pcov

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for dir in packages/*; do
            composer install --working-dir="$dir" --no-interaction --prefer-dist
          done

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for dir in packages/*; do
            composer check-platform-reqs --working-dir="$dir"
          done

      - name: Restore the DocGen cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
        with:
          path: build/docgen-cache
          key: docgen-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('packages/*/composer.lock') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            docgen-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('packages/*/composer.lock') }}-
            docgen-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Generate the coverage report the site reads
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for dir in packages/*; do
            composer --working-dir="$dir" test:coverage
          done

      - name: Generate the documentation
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          repository="$(printf '%s' "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
          php packages/docgen-php/bin/docgen --packages=packages/* --exclude='*/tests/PhpStan/*,*/tests/Doctest/*,*/tests/TestReporter/*' --base-url="https://${repository%%/*}.github.io/${repository#*/}"

      - name: Check out the documentation branch
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DOCS_BRANCH }}
          path: .docs-branch

      - name: Publish the site
        working-directory: .docs-branch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          rsync -a --checksum --delete --exclude '/.git/' --exclude '/pr/' --exclude '/CNAME' ../build/docs/ ./

          git add --all
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "The ${DOCS_BRANCH} branch already serves this documentation."
            exit 0
          fi

          git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
            commit --message "docs: generate from ${GITHUB_SHA}"
          git push origin "HEAD:${DOCS_BRANCH}"

name: Context7

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  refresh:
    name: Refresh the Context7 library
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Request a refresh of the indexed documentation
        env:
          CONTEXT7_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CONTEXT7_API_KEY }}
          LIBRARY_NAME: /${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          if [ -z "${CONTEXT7_API_KEY}" ]; then
            echo '::error::The CONTEXT7_API_KEY repository secret is not set. Copy the key from https://context7.com/dashboard into Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions.'
            exit 1
          fi

          response_file="$(mktemp)"
          status="$(curl --silent --show-error --output "${response_file}" --write-out '%{http_code}' \
            --request POST https://context7.com/api/v1/refresh \
            --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --header "Authorization: Bearer ${CONTEXT7_API_KEY}" \
            --data "{\"libraryName\": \"${LIBRARY_NAME}\"}")"
          echo "HTTP ${status}: $(cat "${response_file}")"

          if [ "${status}" = '200' ]; then
            exit 0
          fi

          error_code="$(jq -r '.error // empty' "${response_file}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [ "${status}" = '400' ] && [ "${error_code}" = 'too-early' ]; then
            echo "::notice::Context7 declined the refresh of ${LIBRARY_NAME} because its minimum interval since the last update has not passed. The next push after that interval refreshes the library."
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "::error::Context7 rejected the refresh of ${LIBRARY_NAME} with HTTP ${status}. Check the response above: 401 means the CONTEXT7_API_KEY secret is wrong, 404 means the library is not registered under that name."
          exit 1

name: Renovate lock files

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths:
      - packages/*/composer.json
      - packages/*/composer.lock

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: renovate-lockfiles-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  refresh:
    name: Refresh the PHP compatibility lock files
    if: >-
      (github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'renovate[bot]' ||
       github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'mend-for-github-com[bot]') &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      startsWith(github.head_ref, 'renovate/') &&
      github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: read
      actions: write
    env:
      COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'
    steps:
      - name: Check out the Renovate revision
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.5'
          extensions: mbstring, pcntl, gd
          coverage: none

      - name: Resolve dependencies for each supported PHP version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # Global platform overrides preserve each manifest's content hash.
          # No packages are installed and no repository or dependency scripts run.
          originals=()
          for dir in packages/*; do
            original="$(mktemp)"
            cp "$dir/composer.lock" "${original}"
            originals+=("${dir}|${original}")
          done
          restore_locks() {
            local entry dir original
            for entry in "${originals[@]}"; do
              dir="${entry%%|*}"
              original="${entry#*|}"
              cp "${original}" "$dir/composer.lock"
              rm -f "${original}"
            done
          }
          trap restore_locks EXIT

          for php_version in 8.0 8.1 8.2 8.3 8.4; do
            composer --no-plugins config --global platform.php "${php_version}.0"
            for dir in packages/*; do
              cp "$dir/composer.lock.php-${php_version}" "$dir/composer.lock"
              composer update --no-install --no-scripts --no-plugins --prefer-dist --working-dir="$dir"
              composer validate --strict --no-check-publish --working-dir="$dir"
              cp "$dir/composer.lock" "$dir/composer.lock.php-${php_version}"
            done
          done

      - name: Commit the lock files and run CI on the new revision
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          HEAD_BRANCH: ${{ github.head_ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          git add packages/*/composer.lock.php-*
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo 'The compatibility lock files are already current.'
            exit 0
          fi

          current_pr="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}")"
          if [ "$(jq -r '.state' <<< "${current_pr}")" != 'open' ] ||
             [ "$(jq -r '.head.sha' <<< "${current_pr}")" != "${EXPECTED_SHA}" ]; then
            echo 'The PR changed while dependencies were resolving; leaving the new revision untouched.'
            exit 0
          fi

          git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
            commit --message 'chore(deps): refresh PHP compatibility lock files'
          git push origin "HEAD:${HEAD_BRANCH}"

          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes do not start CI automatically. Dispatch explicitly
          # so Renovate sees checks for the commit containing the refreshed locks.
          gh workflow run ci.yml --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --ref "${HEAD_BRANCH}"

33	The corresponding private key is a repository Actions secret in the monorepo:
34

42	| `phpunit-ai-reporter` | `SPLIT_PHPUNIT_AI_REPORTER_SSH_KEY` |

44	To rotate a key, generate an Ed25519 key pair, add its public key as a writable
45	deploy key on that mirror, replace the matching Actions secret with the private
46	key, verify a manual split run, and then remove the old deploy key. Each key can

# Publishing the Composer packages

Development takes place on `main` in `k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit`. Each directory in
`packages/` has a public mirror at `https://github.com/k-kinzal/<directory>`.
Submit these six mirror URLs to [Packagist](https://packagist.org/packages/submit),
not the monorepo URL. Submit `docgen-php`, `doctest-php`, `guard-php`, and
`phpunit-ai-reporter` before the PHPStan packages, which depend on them.

The [Split Monorepo workflow](../.github/workflows/split.yml) validates the
distribution archives and installs all six packages in a fresh consumer project
on PHP 8.0 and 8.5 before publishing. It runs on pushes to `main`, stable `v*`
tags, and manual dispatches. Pull requests only run validation.

## What is published

Each mirror contains the committed package directory, with these changes:

- Remove monorepo path repositories and every development lock file.
- Set internal package dependencies to `dev-main` on main, or `^MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`
  for a release. All six packages share the same release version.
- Add documentation, source, and issue tracker URLs to Composer metadata.
- Add a mirror notice to the README and omit tests and development tool
  configuration from GitHub distribution archives using `.gitattributes`.

The original manifests and lock files stay in the monorepo for development.
Do not edit the mirrors: the next synchronization replaces their files. Existing
commits remain in their history. The existing `doctest-php` repository is reused
with its earlier history intact.

## Authentication

Each mirror has a write-enabled SSH deploy key named `php-ai-toolkit split`.
The corresponding private key is a repository Actions secret in the monorepo:

| Mirror | Actions secret |
| --- | --- |
| `docgen-php` | `SPLIT_DOCGEN_PHP_SSH_KEY` |
| `doctest-php` | `SPLIT_DOCTEST_PHP_SSH_KEY` |
| `guard-php` | `SPLIT_GUARD_PHP_SSH_KEY` |
| `phpstan-ai-formatter` | `SPLIT_PHPSTAN_AI_FORMATTER_SSH_KEY` |
| `phpstan-guard-rules` | `SPLIT_PHPSTAN_GUARD_RULES_SSH_KEY` |
| `phpunit-ai-reporter` | `SPLIT_PHPUNIT_AI_REPORTER_SSH_KEY` |

To rotate a key, generate an Ed25519 key pair, add its public key as a writable
deploy key on that mirror, replace the matching Actions secret with the private
key, verify a manual split run, and then remove the old deploy key. Each key can
write only to its own mirror; the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` only reads the monorepo.

## Releasing

The planned first release is `0.1.0`. Initial setup publishes only `main`; it does
not create a release tag. Packagist can index that branch as `dev-main`.

Wait for CI to pass on the intended `main` commit, then create and push an
annotated stable tag on the monorepo, for example:

```sh
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m 'Release v0.1.0'
git push origin v0.1.0
```

The split workflow creates the same tag in all six mirrors. Tag snapshots do not
move mirror `main` branches, so publishing an older release cannot roll back
development. Re-running a tag succeeds if its files already match and fails if
the tag would change. Publish a new version instead of moving existing tags.
Wait for each release run to finish before pushing the next release tag.

After the first successful split, submit each mirror on Packagist. Connect the
[Packagist GitHub hook](https://packagist.org/about#how-to-update-packages) so later
pushes update the package automatically. Until a stable tag exists, consumers
must explicitly allow `dev-main` for every toolkit dependency they use.

## Local verification

Run `bash .github/scripts/test-split.sh` with PHP, Composer, Git, jq, and rsync
installed. It builds archives from `HEAD`, checks Composer publication metadata,
installs both development and stable distributions, exercises the CLI entry
points, and tests synchronization against a temporary local Git remote.

# guard-php

[![PHP](https://img.shields.io/badge/php-8.0%2B-777bb4?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://www.php.net/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

Check and repair PHP project policies for source metrics, directory structure,
Markdown documents, and tool configuration.

## Requirements

- PHP 8.0 or later

## Getting Started

```console
$ composer require --dev k-kinzal/guard-php
$ vendor/bin/guard --help
guard 1.0.0

Checks and repairs a project against the policies in its guard.yaml. Running guard without a command runs check.

Usage:
  command [options] [arguments]

Options:
  -h, --help            Display help for the given command, or list the commands when none is given
      --silent          Do not output any message
  -q, --quiet           Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed
  -V, --version         Display this application version
      --ansi|--no-ansi  Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output
  -n, --no-interaction  Do not ask any interactive question
  -v|vv|vvv, --verbose  Increase the verbosity of messages: 1 for normal output, 2 for more verbose output and 3 for debug

Available commands:
  baseline    Record current violations in a baseline for subsequent checks
  check       Check the project against its policy without changing any file
  completion  Dump the shell completion script
  fix         Repair the violations guard can fix, then report what remains
  help        Display help for a command
  init        Create a policy file with the presets that fit the project
  list        List commands
  rules       List active rules, their messages and automatic fix support
```

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

9	  contents: read

12	  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
