1	# PHPStan Rules
2	
3	Custom PHPStan rules provided by php-ai-toolkit. Each rule detects anti-patterns that actually occur in AI-generated code.
4	
5	## Rector Support
6	
7	Every rule below is classified as **Safe**, **Risky**, or **Unavailable** for automatic
8	changes. Enable the safe group with `withRules(SafeRules::rules())` or the risky
9	group with `withRules(RiskyRules::rules())` in `rector.php`. Both classes are in
10	`Toolkit\Rector`; their lists can be combined, and individual Rector classes can
11	also be registered with `withRules()`.
12	A classification describes only the supported cases; each rule’s Rector section
13	lists skipped cases and review requirements.
14	
15	The legacy opt-in [ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule](rules/ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule.md#rector)
16	is also classified as **Unavailable**. Internal helper rules for mixed types and
17	class dispatch share their parent rule’s classification.
18	
19	## General
20	
21	Rules applied to all code.
22	
23	| Rule | Description | Error Identifier | Rector |
24	|------|-------------|------------------|--------|
25	| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md) | Forbids `@phpstan-ignore` and `@infection-ignore-all` comments | `customRules.phpstanIgnoreComment`, `customRules.infectionIgnoreAllComment` | [Risky](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) |
26	| [ForbidFileTermRule](rules/ForbidFileTermRule.md) | Forbids configured literal terms in files matching restricted path patterns | `customRules.forbiddenFileTerm` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidFileTermRule.md#rector) |
27	| [ForbidDependencyRule](rules/ForbidDependencyRule.md) | Forbids symbol and file-reading dependencies between configured paths; allows each root directory to depend only on itself and src by default | `customRules.forbiddenDependency` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidDependencyRule.md#rector) |
28	| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md) | Forbids direct calls to magic methods | `customRules.forbiddenMagicMethodCall` | [Risky](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) |
29	| [ForbiddenNamespaceRule](rules/ForbiddenNamespaceRule.md) | Forbids configured namespace prefixes and whole segments at any depth, including `Model`, `Models`, `Infrastructure`, and `Infrastructures` by default | `customRules.forbiddenNamespace` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbiddenNamespaceRule.md#rector) |
30	| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md) | Requires `#[Override]` attribute on overridden methods | `customRules.overrideMustHaveAttribute` | [Safe](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) |
31	| [SrcUnitTestPairRule](rules/SrcUnitTestPairRule.md) | Enforces 1:1 pairing between `src/` classes and `tests/Unit/` test classes | `customRules.srcUnitTestPair` | [Unavailable](rules/SrcUnitTestPairRule.md#rector) |
32	| [RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule](rules/RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule.md) | Requires PHPDoc on all public API elements | `customRules.requirePhpDocOnPublicApi` | [Unavailable](rules/RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule.md#rector) |
33	| [RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule](rules/RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule.md) | Requires a runnable `@example` on declarations marked `@visibility public` | `customRules.requireExampleOnClass`, `customRules.requireExampleOnMethod`, `customRules.requireExampleOnProperty`, `customRules.requireExampleOnConstant`, `customRules.requireExampleOnEnumCase` | [Unavailable](rules/RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule.md#rector) |
34	| [EnforceVisibilityScopeRule](rules/EnforceVisibilityScopeRule.md) | Enforces namespace visibility scopes declared with `@visibility` and treats explicitly public API as externally used | `customRules.visibilityInvalidScope`, `customRules.visibilityOutOfScope` | [Unavailable](rules/EnforceVisibilityScopeRule.md#rector) |
35	| [EnforceMutationContractRule](rules/EnforceMutationContractRule.md) | Makes parameter, receiver, and global mutation explicit and propagates effects through statically resolved calls | `customRules.mutationInvalidContract`, `customRules.mutationUndeclared`, `customRules.mutationOverrideWidened` | [Unavailable](rules/EnforceMutationContractRule.md#rector) |
36	| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md) | Forbids `/* */` and `#` comments everywhere, and `//` comments outside `catch` blocks and array literals; `/** */` PHPDoc is allowed | `customRules.forbidNonDocComment` | [Risky](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) |
37	| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md) | Forbids single-line PHPDoc on public elements; requires multi-line format | `customRules.forbidSingleLinePhpDoc` | [Safe](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md#rector) |
38	| [ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule](rules/ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule.md) | Forbids configured suffixes on class, interface, trait, and enum names | `customRules.forbiddenClassLikeNameSuffix` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule.md#rector) |
39	| [NoNonPublicMethodRule](rules/NoNonPublicMethodRule.md) | Forbids private methods and forbids protected methods outside abstract classes, traits, and override methods; constructors are exempt | `customRules.nonPublicMethod` | [Unavailable](rules/NoNonPublicMethodRule.md#rector) |
40	| [ForbidEmptyCatchRule](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md) | Forbids catch blocks with an empty body | `customRules.emptyCatch` | [Risky](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md#rector) |
41	| [RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md) | Requires `@throws` for exceptions thrown directly in a method and not caught within it | `customRules.missingThrowsTag` | [Risky](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md#rector) |
42	| [RequireExceptionChainingRule](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md) | Requires new exceptions thrown inside catch blocks to chain the caught exception | `customRules.unchainedRethrow` | [Risky](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md#rector) |
43	| [ForbidBroadCatchRule](rules/ForbidBroadCatchRule.md) | Forbids catching `Throwable`, `Exception`, and the `LogicException`/`Error` families outside configured boundary paths | `customRules.broadCatch` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidBroadCatchRule.md#rector) |
44	| [ForbidGenericThrowsTagRule](rules/ForbidGenericThrowsTagRule.md) | Forbids `@throws \Exception` and `@throws \Throwable` tags | `customRules.genericThrowsTag` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidGenericThrowsTagRule.md#rector) |
45	| [ForbidInternalMixedTypeRule](rules/ForbidInternalMixedTypeRule.md) | Forbids explicit concrete `mixed` in internal declarations while allowing public, inherited, magic-protocol, and template contracts | `customRules.internalMixedType` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidInternalMixedTypeRule.md#rector) |
46	| [RequireListForArrayLiteralRule](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md) | Requires `list<V>` instead of `array<int, V>` when a property or callable visibly owns a non-empty list literal; input parameters remain unrestricted | `customRules.arrayLiteralListType` | [Risky](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md#rector) |
47	| [RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule](rules/RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule.md) | Requires a `switch` or `match` that names its subject — `match ($suit)`, or `match ($payment::class)` for a sealed hierarchy — to name a branch for every value that subject can hold, the way Rust and Kotlin check a match over a closed type | `customRules.exhaustiveDispatch`, `customRules.exhaustiveDispatchDefault` | [Unavailable](rules/RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule.md#rector) |
48	
49	## Test Class
50	
51	Rules applied to test classes in the `Tests\Unit` / `Tests\Integration` namespaces. Rules marked with `*` apply to all `Tests\` namespaces.
52	
53	| Rule | Description | Error Identifier | Rector |
54	|------|-------------|------------------|--------|
55	| [NoPropertyInTestClassRule](rules/NoPropertyInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids property declarations in test classes | `customRules.noPropertyInTestClass` | [Unavailable](rules/NoPropertyInTestClassRule.md#rector) |
56	| [NoClassConstantInTestClassRule](rules/NoClassConstantInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids class constants in test classes | `customRules.noClassConstantInTestClass` | [Unavailable](rules/NoClassConstantInTestClassRule.md#rector) |
57	| [NoPrivateMethodInTestClassRule](rules/NoPrivateMethodInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids private methods in test classes | `customRules.noPrivateMethodInTestClass` | [Unavailable](rules/NoPrivateMethodInTestClassRule.md#rector) |
58	| [NoHelperMethodInTestClassRule](rules/NoHelperMethodInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids methods other than test/provider/override | `customRules.noHelperMethodInTestClass` | [Unavailable](rules/NoHelperMethodInTestClassRule.md#rector) |
59	| [NoControlFlowInTestMethodRule](rules/NoControlFlowInTestMethodRule.md) | Forbids control flow statements in test methods | `customRules.noControlFlowInTestMethod` | [Unavailable](rules/NoControlFlowInTestMethodRule.md#rector) |
60	| [NoTraitUseInTestClassRule](rules/NoTraitUseInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids trait usage in test classes | `customRules.noTraitUseInTestClass` | [Unavailable](rules/NoTraitUseInTestClassRule.md#rector) |
61	| [NoReflectionInTestClassRule](rules/NoReflectionInTestClassRule.md) `*` | Forbids Reflection API usage in test classes | `customRules.noReflectionInTestClass` | [Unavailable](rules/NoReflectionInTestClassRule.md#rector) |
62	| [NoRedundantAssertInstanceOfRule](rules/NoRedundantAssertInstanceOfRule.md) `*` | Forbids redundant PHPUnit `assertInstanceOf()` calls for values with one statically-known type | `customRules.noRedundantAssertInstanceOf` | [Unavailable](rules/NoRedundantAssertInstanceOfRule.md#rector) |
63	| [NoBrokenCodeExpectationRule](rules/NoBrokenCodeExpectationRule.md) `*` | Forbids `expectException()` / `expectExceptionObject()` for `Throwable` and the `LogicException`/`Error` families | `customRules.noBrokenCodeExpectation` | [Unavailable](rules/NoBrokenCodeExpectationRule.md#rector) |
64	| [PhpUnitMockApiRule](rules/PhpUnitMockApiRule.md) `*` | Restricts mock API and enforces interface-only mocking | `customRules.phpUnitMockApi` | [Unavailable](rules/PhpUnitMockApiRule.md#rector) |
65	| [ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids descriptive PHPDoc text in test classes | `customRules.forbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClass` | [Risky](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md#rector) |
66	| [TestNamingConventionRule](rules/TestNamingConventionRule.md) | Enforces naming conventions for test methods and data providers | `customRules.testNamingConvention` | [Unavailable](rules/TestNamingConventionRule.md#rector) |
67	
68	## Enabling and Disabling Rules
69	
70	Rules inherit `toolkit.allRules`, which defaults to `true`, except mutation
71	contracts, which are opt-in so an existing unannotated project does not change
72	semantics on upgrade. Override a specific rule through its `enabled` value:
73	
74	```neon
75	parameters:
76	    toolkit:
77	        forbidEmptyCatch:
78	            enabled: false
79	```
80	
81	Set `allRules: false` to make every rule opt-in. Toolkit adoption keeps the
82	default; changing a switch is an explicit project policy decision.
83	
84	Enable mutation contracts explicitly with `toolkit.mutation.enabled: true`.
85	
86	## Redundant PHPStan Diagnostics
87	
88	The toolkit suppresses a PHPStan or Strict Rules diagnostic only when an enabled
89	toolkit rule makes that diagnostic non-actionable. The toolkit error remains as
90	the single instruction for fixing the prohibited construct:
91	
92	| Enabled toolkit rule | Suppressed diagnostic | Scope |
93	|----------------------|-----------------------|-------|
94	| `noNonPublicMethod` | `method.unused`, `method.finalPrivate` | Private method declarations; PHPStan does not emit either for constructors, and `consistentConstructor.private` stays visible because the rule exempts constructors |
95	| `noPrivateMethodInTestClass` | The same private-method diagnostics | Restricted test classes |
96	| `noPropertyInTestClass` | `property.unused`, `property.neverRead`, `property.neverWritten`, `property.onlyRead`, `property.onlyWritten` | Restricted test classes |
97	| `noClassConstantInTestClass` | `classConstant.unused` | Restricted test classes |
98	| `noControlFlowInTestMethod` | PHPStan and Strict Rules diagnostics emitted for the prohibited `if`, loop, `switch`, or `match` node | Test methods in restricted test classes |
99	| `requireThrowsTagOnDirectThrow` | `missingType.checkedException` | Direct escaping throws in methods; propagated checked exceptions remain reported |
100	
101	This is semantic suppression through PHPStan's extension API, not a global
102	`ignoreErrors` entry. Disabling the dominating toolkit rule automatically
103	restores the corresponding PHPStan diagnostics. Independent findings remain
104	visible; for example, an unused private property in production code and a dead
105	broad catch are still reported.
106	
107	## Parameters
108	
109	The following values can be customized under `parameters.toolkit` in a project's
110	`phpstan.neon`:
111	
112	| Parameter | Default | Description |
113	|-----------|---------|-------------|
114	| `testNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests']` | Test namespace prefixes |
115	| `restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests\Unit', 'Tests\Integration']` | Test namespaces where strict rules apply |
116	| `visibilityExemptNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests']` | Namespace subtrees allowed to reference declarations across `@visibility` boundaries |
117	| `srcUnitTestPairExcludePatterns` | `[]` | Patterns to exclude from test pair checks |
118	| `srcMarker` | `'/src/'` | Source code path marker |
119	| `unitTestMarker` | `'/tests/Unit/'` | Unit test path marker |
120	| `forbiddenTermsByPath` | `[]` | Map of restricted file path patterns to case-insensitive literal terms forbidden anywhere in matching files |
121	| `dependencyProjectRoot` | `%currentWorkingDirectory%` | Absolute root for dependency boundary patterns |
122	| `forbiddenDependencies` | Root directories may depend on themselves and `src/**`; `vendor/**` and root files are exempt | Directed `from`/`to` path policies with optional `excludeFrom`, `excludeTo`, and `allowSameRootDirectory` |
123	| `dependencyFileReaders` | `[]` | Additional function or `Class::method` file readers with argument `position` and `name`; built-ins remain active |
124	| `forbiddenNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests\Support', 'Tests\Supports', 'Tests\Helper', 'Tests\Helpers', 'Tests\Util', 'Tests\Utils', 'Tests\Utility', 'Tests\Utilities', 'Tests\Fixture', 'Tests\Fixtures']` | Namespace prefixes to forbid |
125	| `forbiddenNamespaceSegments` | `['Model', 'Models', 'Infrastructure', 'Infrastructures']` | Whole namespace segments to forbid at any depth; matching is case-sensitive |
126	| `forbiddenClassLikeNameSuffixes` | See [`rules.neon`](../rules.neon) | Class-like declaration name suffixes to forbid |
127	| `broadCatchAllowedPaths` | `[]` | fnmatch patterns of boundary files allowed to catch `Throwable`, `Exception`, and the `LogicException`/`Error` families |

## Enabling and Disabling Rules

Rules inherit `toolkit.allRules`, which defaults to `true`, except mutation
contracts, which are opt-in so an existing unannotated project does not change
semantics on upgrade. Override a specific rule through its `enabled` value:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        forbidEmptyCatch:
            enabled: false
```

Set `allRules: false` to make every rule opt-in. Toolkit adoption keeps the
default; changing a switch is an explicit project policy decision.

Enable mutation contracts explicitly with `toolkit.mutation.enabled: true`.

## Redundant PHPStan Diagnostics

The toolkit suppresses a PHPStan or Strict Rules diagnostic only when an enabled
toolkit rule makes that diagnostic non-actionable. The toolkit error remains as
the single instruction for fixing the prohibited construct:

| Enabled toolkit rule | Suppressed diagnostic | Scope |
|----------------------|-----------------------|-------|
| `noNonPublicMethod` | `method.unused`, `method.finalPrivate` | Private method declarations; PHPStan does not emit either for constructors, and `consistentConstructor.private` stays visible because the rule exempts constructors |
| `noPrivateMethodInTestClass` | The same private-method diagnostics | Restricted test classes |
| `noPropertyInTestClass` | `property.unused`, `property.neverRead`, `property.neverWritten`, `property.onlyRead`, `property.onlyWritten` | Restricted test classes |
| `noClassConstantInTestClass` | `classConstant.unused` | Restricted test classes |
| `noControlFlowInTestMethod` | PHPStan and Strict Rules diagnostics emitted for the prohibited `if`, loop, `switch`, or `match` node | Test methods in restricted test classes |
| `requireThrowsTagOnDirectThrow` | `missingType.checkedException` | Direct escaping throws in methods; propagated checked exceptions remain reported |

This is semantic suppression through PHPStan's extension API, not a global
`ignoreErrors` entry. Disabling the dominating toolkit rule automatically
restores the corresponding PHPStan diagnostics. Independent findings remain
visible; for example, an unused private property in production code and a dead
broad catch are still reported.

## Parameters

The following values can be customized under `parameters.toolkit` in a project's
`phpstan.neon`:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `testNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests']` | Test namespace prefixes |
| `restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests\Unit', 'Tests\Integration']` | Test namespaces where strict rules apply |
| `visibilityExemptNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests']` | Namespace subtrees allowed to reference declarations across `@visibility` boundaries |
| `srcUnitTestPairExcludePatterns` | `[]` | Patterns to exclude from test pair checks |
| `srcMarker` | `'/src/'` | Source code path marker |
| `unitTestMarker` | `'/tests/Unit/'` | Unit test path marker |
| `forbiddenTermsByPath` | `[]` | Map of restricted file path patterns to case-insensitive literal terms forbidden anywhere in matching files |
| `dependencyProjectRoot` | `%currentWorkingDirectory%` | Absolute root for dependency boundary patterns |
| `forbiddenDependencies` | Root directories may depend on themselves and `src/**`; `vendor/**` and root files are exempt | Directed `from`/`to` path policies with optional `excludeFrom`, `excludeTo`, and `allowSameRootDirectory` |
| `dependencyFileReaders` | `[]` | Additional function or `Class::method` file readers with argument `position` and `name`; built-ins remain active |
| `forbiddenNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests\Support', 'Tests\Supports', 'Tests\Helper', 'Tests\Helpers', 'Tests\Util', 'Tests\Utils', 'Tests\Utility', 'Tests\Utilities', 'Tests\Fixture', 'Tests\Fixtures']` | Namespace prefixes to forbid |
| `forbiddenNamespaceSegments` | `['Model', 'Models', 'Infrastructure', 'Infrastructures']` | Whole namespace segments to forbid at any depth; matching is case-sensitive |
| `forbiddenClassLikeNameSuffixes` | See [`rules.neon`](../rules.neon) | Class-like declaration name suffixes to forbid |
| `broadCatchAllowedPaths` | `[]` | fnmatch patterns of boundary files allowed to catch `Throwable`, `Exception`, and the `LogicException`/`Error` families |

namespace Guard\Reporting;

use Guard\Diagnostic\Finding;
use Guard\Policy\FileChange;
use Guard\Reporting\Filtering\ReportScope;
use JsonException;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Formatter\OutputFormatter;

/**
 * Renders human diagnostics, compact AI diagnostics and structured reports.
 */
final class Reporter
{
    /**
     * @param list<Finding> $findings
     */
    public function hasErrors(array $findings): bool
    {
        foreach ($findings as $finding) {
            if ($finding->level === 'required') {
                return true;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }

    /**
     * @param list<Finding> $findings
     * @param list<FileChange> $changes
     * @throws JsonException
     */
    public function render(array $findings, array $changes, string $format, string $action, bool $decorated = false, ?ReportScope $scope = null): string
    {
        $rows = [];
        foreach ($findings as $finding) {
            $rows[] = ['path' => $finding->path, 'rule' => $finding->rule, 'level' => $finding->level === 'required' ? 'error' : 'warning',
                'message' => $finding->message, 'fixable' => $finding->fixable];
        }
        $diffs = [];
        foreach ($changes as $change) {
            $diffs[] = ['path' => $change->path, 'diff' => (new ChangeDiff())->render($change)];
        }
        if ($format === 'json') {
            return json_encode(['findings' => $rows, 'changes' => array_column($diffs, 'path'), 'diffs' => $diffs,
                'action' => $action, 'success' => !$this->hasErrors($scope === null ? $findings : $scope->findings), 'summary' => $this->counts($findings)] + ($scope === null ? [] : [
                    'selection' => ['shown' => count($findings), 'total' => count($scope->findings), 'hidden' => count($scope->findings) - count($findings)],
                    'totalSummary' => $this->counts($scope->findings),
                    'baseline' => $scope->baseline === null ? null : ['path' => $scope->baseline, 'suppressed' => $scope->suppressed, 'unmatched' => $scope->unmatched],
                ]), JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR | JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE) . "\n";
        }
        if ($format === 'ai') {
            return $this->ai($findings, $changes, $action, $scope);
        }
        return $this->human($findings, $changes, $action, $decorated, $scope);
    }

    /**
     * @param list<Finding> $findings
     * @return array{errors: int, warnings: int, fixable: int}
     */
    public function counts(array $findings): array
    {
        $counts = ['errors' => 0, 'warnings' => 0, 'fixable' => 0];
        foreach ($findings as $finding) {
            ++$counts[$finding->level === 'required' ? 'errors' : 'warnings'];
            if ($finding->fixable) {
                ++$counts['fixable'];
            }
        }
        return $counts;
    }

    /**
     * @param list<Finding> $findings
     * @param list<FileChange> $changes
     */
    public function ai(array $findings, array $changes, string $action, ?ReportScope $scope = null): string
    {
        $lines = [];
        foreach ($findings as $finding) {
            $lines[] = sprintf('%s: %s [%s] fixable=%s %s', $finding->level === 'required' ? 'error' : 'warning', $finding->path, $finding->rule, $finding->fixable ? 'yes' : 'no', $finding->message);
        }
        foreach ($changes as $change) {
            $lines[] = $action . ': ' . $change->path;
            $lines[] = rtrim((new ChangeDiff())->render($change), "\n");
        }
        $lines[] = $this->actionNote($action);
        $lines[] = $this->summary($findings, $changes, $action, ', ') . '.';
        $lines[] = $scope === null ? '' : $scope->note(count($findings));
        $lines[] = $this->hasErrors($scope === null ? $findings : $scope->findings) ? 'Guard found required violations.' : 'Guard passed.';
        return implode("\n", array_filter($lines, static fn (string $line): bool => $line !== '')) . "\n";
    }

    /**
     * @param list<Finding> $findings
     * @param list<FileChange> $changes
     */
    public function human(array $findings, array $changes, string $action, bool $decorated, ?ReportScope $scope = null): string
    {
        $formatter = new OutputFormatter($decorated);
        $title = $action === 'checked' ? 'Guard check' : 'Guard fix';
        $lines = ['', '<options=bold>' . $title . '</>', ''];
        $groups = [];
        foreach ($findings as $finding) {
            $groups[$finding->path][] = $finding;
        }
        foreach ($groups as $group) {
            $lines[] = '<options=bold>' . OutputFormatter::escape($group[0]->path) . '</>';
            foreach ($group as $finding) {
                $level = $finding->level === 'required' ? 'error' : 'warning';
                $color = $finding->level === 'required' ? 'red' : 'yellow';
                $lines[] = sprintf('  <fg=%s>%s:</> %s  <fg=cyan>%s</>', $color, $level, OutputFormatter::escape($finding->rule), $finding->fixable ? 'fixable' : 'manual');
                $lines[] = '    ' . OutputFormatter::escape($finding->message);
            }
            $lines[] = '';
        }
        foreach ($changes as $change) {
            $lines[] = '<options=bold>' . OutputFormatter::escape($action . ': ' . $change->path) . '</>';
            foreach (explode("\n", rtrim((new ChangeDiff())->render($change), "\n")) as $line) {
                $color = str_starts_with($line, '+') ? 'green' : (str_starts_with($line, '-') ? 'red' : 'default');
                $lines[] = '  <fg=' . $color . '>' . OutputFormatter::escape($line) . '</>';
            }
            $lines[] = '';
        }
        $counts = $this->counts($findings);
        $lines[] = '<options=bold>' . $this->summary($findings, $changes, $action, ' · ') . '</>';
        if ($this->actionNote($action) !== '') {
            $lines[] = $this->actionNote($action);
        }
        if ($counts['fixable'] > 0 && $action === 'checked') {
            $lines[] = 'Preview repairs: guard fix --dry-run';
        }
        if ($scope !== null && $scope->note(count($findings)) !== '') {
            $lines[] = OutputFormatter::escape($scope->note(count($findings)));
        }
        $lines[] = $this->hasErrors($scope === null ? $findings : $scope->findings) ? '<fg=red>Guard found required violations.</>' : '<fg=green>Guard passed.</>';
        return $formatter->format(implode("\n", $lines) . "\n") ?? '';
    }

    /**
     * @param list<Finding> $findings
     * @param list<FileChange> $changes
     */
    public function summary(array $findings, array $changes, string $action, string $separator): string
    {
        $counts = $this->counts($findings);
        $files = $action === 'checked' ? count(array_unique(array_map(static fn (Finding $finding): string => $finding->path, $findings))) : count($changes);
        return implode($separator, [
            $counts['errors'] . ($counts['errors'] === 1 ? ' error' : ' errors'),
            $counts['warnings'] . ($counts['warnings'] === 1 ? ' warning' : ' warnings'),
            $counts['fixable'] . ' fixable',
            $files . ($files === 1 ? ' file ' : ' files ') . ($action === 'checked' ? 'with findings' : $action),
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * Explains whether the plan was written, previewed, or blocked.
     */
    public function actionNote(string $action): string
    {
        return match ($action) {
            'blocked' => 'Repairs blocked by required configuration violations. No files were written; diffs show the proposed changes.',
            'would change' => 'Dry run: no files were written. Run guard fix to apply these changes.',
            default => '',
        };
    }
}

final class RegistrationTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testRegisteredPolicyDeclaresFilesAndCliReportsItsFindings(): void
    {
        $project = new class (['guard.yaml' => "version: 1\nstructure: {paths: [.], directories: []}\n"]) {
            public string $root;
            /**
             * @param array<array-key, string> $files
             */
            public function __construct(array $files = [])
            {
                $this->root = sys_get_temp_dir() . '/guard-contract-' . uniqid('', true);
                mkdir($this->root);
                foreach ($files as $path => $source) {
                    $this->write((string) $path, $source);
                }
            }
            public function write(string $path, string $source): void
            {
                $directory = dirname($this->root . '/' . $path);
                if (!is_dir($directory)) {
                    mkdir($directory, 0777, true);
                }
                file_put_contents($this->root . '/' . $path, $source);
            }
            public function remove(): void
            {
                foreach (new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($this->root, FilesystemIterator::SKIP_DOTS), RecursiveIteratorIterator::CHILD_FIRST) as $file) {
                    if ($file instanceof SplFileInfo) {
                        if ($file->isDir() && !$file->isLink()) {
                            rmdir($file->getPathname());
                        } else {
                            unlink($file->getPathname());
                        }
                    }
                }
                rmdir($this->root);
            }
        };
        try {
            $registry = Registry::defaults();
            $registry->addPolicy('readme', new class (['readme' => new Input(new Selection('files', ['README.md'], [], '', false, ''), null)], static function (InputSet $inputs, Context $context): Plan {
                $file = $inputs->get('readme')->files['README.md'] ?? null;
                $exists = $file === null || $file->file->entry->file;
                return new Plan($exists ? [] : [new Finding('README.md', 'readme.required', 'required', 'Create README.md.')], []);
            }) implements Policy
            {
                /** @param array<string, Input> $inputs
                 * @param Closure(InputSet, Context): Plan $callback
                 */
                public function __construct(private array $inputs, private Closure $callback)
                {
                }
                public function inputs(Context $context): array
                {
                    return $this->inputs;
                }
                public function evaluate(InputSet $inputs, Context $context): Plan
                {
                    return ($this->callback)($inputs, $context);
                }
            });

            $output = '';
            $app = new Application($project->root, static function (string $text) use (&$output): void {
                $output .= $text;
            }, $registry);
            self::assertSame(1, $app->run(['check', '--format=ai']));
            self::assertStringContainsString('[readme.required]', $output);
            $project->write('README.md', '# Project');
            self::assertSame(0, $app->run(['check']));
        } finally {
            $project->remove();
        }
    }

    public function testConfiguredPoliciesAndStructurersShareScopeAndCanRunRepeatedly(): void
    {
        $structurer = new class () implements Structurer {
            public function __construct(private string $prefix = '')
            {
            }
            public function structure(Source $source): Text
            {
                return new Text($this->prefix . $source->text());
            }
        };
        $policy = new class () implements Policy {
            public function __construct(private string $structure = 'text', private string $expected = 'ok')
            {
            }
            public function inputs(Context $context): array
            {
                return ['text' => new Input(new Selection('patterns', ['*.txt']), $this->structure)];
            }
            /**
             * @throws JsonException
             * @throws Exception
             */
            public function evaluate(InputSet $inputs, Context $context): Plan
            {
                $findings = [];
                foreach ($inputs->get('text')->files as $path => $file) {
                    $text = $file->value();
                    if ($text instanceof Text && $text->content() !== $this->expected) {
                        $findings[] = new Finding($path, 'app.text', 'required', 'Replace the text with ok.');
                    }
                }
                return new Plan($findings, []);
            }
        };
        $root = sys_get_temp_dir() . '/guard-registration-' . uniqid('', true);
        mkdir($root);
        try {
            file_put_contents($root . '/allowed.txt', 'bad');
            file_put_contents($root . '/excluded.txt', 'bad');
            file_put_contents($root . '/guard.yaml', Yaml::dump([
                'version' => 1,
                'collect' => ['include' => ['allowed.txt']],
                'extensions' => [
                    $policy::class => ['expected' => 'prefix:ok', 'structure' => $structurer::class],
                    $structurer::class => ['prefix' => 'prefix:'],
                ],
            ], 6));
            $registry = Registry::defaults();
            $output = '';
            $app = new Application($root, static function (string $text) use (&$output): void {
                $output .= $text;
            }, $registry);
            for ($run = 0; $run < 2; ++$run) {
                $output = '';
                self::assertSame(1, $app->run(['check', '--format=json']));
                self::assertStringContainsString('allowed.txt', $output);
                self::assertStringContainsString('app.text', $output);
                self::assertStringNotContainsString('excluded.txt', $output);
            }
            self::assertSame([], $registry->policies());
            self::assertArrayNotHasKey($structurer::class, $registry->structures());
            file_put_contents($root . '/allowed.txt', 'ok');
            self::assertSame(0, $app->run(['check']));
        } finally {
            unlink($root . '/guard.yaml');
            unlink($root . '/allowed.txt');
            unlink($root . '/excluded.txt');
            rmdir($root);
        }
    }
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	package="${1:?Usage: prepare-package.sh PACKAGE OUTPUT [vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH]}"
5	output="${2:?Pass an empty output directory.}"
6	tag="${3:-}"
7	root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
8	cd "$root"
9	
10	if [[ ! "$package" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]+$ ]] || [ ! -f "packages/$package/composer.json" ]; then
11	  echo "Unknown package '$package'; choose a directory in packages/." >&2
12	  exit 1
13	fi
14	if [ -n "$tag" ] && [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
15	  echo "Invalid release tag '$tag'; use vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, for example v0.1.0." >&2
16	  exit 1
17	fi
18	mkdir -p "$output"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

package="${1:?Usage: prepare-package.sh PACKAGE OUTPUT [vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH]}"
output="${2:?Pass an empty output directory.}"
tag="${3:-}"
root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$root"

if [[ ! "$package" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]+$ ]] || [ ! -f "packages/$package/composer.json" ]; then
  echo "Unknown package '$package'; choose a directory in packages/." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -n "$tag" ] && [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
  echo "Invalid release tag '$tag'; use vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, for example v0.1.0." >&2
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "$output"
if [ -n "$(ls -A "$output")" ]; then
  echo "Output directory '$output' is not empty; prepare into a new directory." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Export committed files only: never copy local vendor/, caches or build output.
git archive "HEAD:packages/$package" | tar -x -C "$output"
names="$(jq -s 'map(.name)' packages/*/composer.json)"
constraint=dev-main
if [ -n "$tag" ]; then
  constraint="^${tag#v}"
fi
jq --argjson names "$names" --arg constraint "$constraint" --arg package "$package" '
  del(.repositories, .version) |
  .homepage = "https://k-kinzal.github.io/php-ai-toolkit/" |
  .support = ((.support // {}) + {
    source: ("https://github.com/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/tree/main/packages/" + $package),
    issues: "https://github.com/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/issues",
    docs: "https://k-kinzal.github.io/php-ai-toolkit/"
  }) |
  (.require, ."require-dev") |= with_entries(
    if (.key as $name | $names | index($name)) != null
    then .value = $constraint else . end
  )
' "$output/composer.json" > "$output/composer.json.tmp"
mv "$output/composer.json.tmp" "$output/composer.json"
rm -f "$output"/composer.lock "$output"/composer.lock.php-*

# Composer's GitHub dist archives should contain the runtime and documentation.
cat >> "$output/.gitattributes" <<'EOF'
/.gitattributes export-ignore
/.gitignore export-ignore
/.php-cs-fixer.dist.php export-ignore
/deptrac.yaml export-ignore
/guard.yaml export-ignore
/infection.json* export-ignore
/phpcs.xml* export-ignore
/phpstan.neon* export-ignore
/phpunit*.xml* export-ignore
/tests/ export-ignore
EOF
cat > "$output/.gitignore" <<'EOF'
/vendor/
/build/
/composer.lock
/.phpunit.cache/
/.phpunit.result.cache
/.php-cs-fixer.cache
/.deptrac.cache
EOF
awk 'NR == 2 {
  print ""
  print "> Read-only mirror of [php-ai-toolkit](https://github.com/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit)."
  print "> Submit changes and issues to the monorepo."
} { print }' "$output/README.md" > "$output/README.md.tmp"
mv "$output/README.md.tmp" "$output/README.md"

composer validate --working-dir="$output" --strict --no-check-lock

# Policies

An AI agent that is asked to make a test pass will also lengthen a method, add a `Helper` class, open a new section in the README or lower the PHPStan level, if nothing stops it. Each of those changes looks reasonable alone. Guard declares what the project has decided about them in `guard.yaml`, reports every change that departs from it, and repairs the departures that have exactly one correct fix.

## Policies

| Section | What it checks | Rule IDs | Repaired by `fix` |
|---------|----------------|----------|---------------------|
| `metrics` | Lines and cyclomatic complexity of PHP files, classes, functions and methods. See [metrics](metrics.md). | `metrics.*` | no |
| `structure` | What each directory may contain, how entries are named, and how many there are. See [structure](structure.md). | `structure.*` | no |
| `documentation` | The headings, outline, badges or exact content of Markdown files, and Markdown files nobody declared. See [documents](documents.md). | `documentation.*` | no |
| `configuration` | Values in the configuration files of other tools, such as `phpstan.neon` or `phpunit.xml.dist`. See [configuration fields](fields.md). | the rule's `id` | yes, when the rule has a repair |
| `extensions` | Whatever a project or a package adds. See [extensions](extensions.md). | chosen by the extension | when the extension proposes a change |

A section that `guard.yaml` neither writes nor [imports](configuration.md#imports) is not checked.

## Required and recommended

Every finding is either required or recommended. A required finding is reported as `error` and fails the command with exit code `1`. A recommendation is reported as `warning` and leaves the exit code at `0`. Configuration rules choose their level with `level`; metric, structure and document findings are always required.

## What is repaired

`guard fix` only writes configuration fields. A field has one value that satisfies its rule, or a declared fallback, so writing it is a deterministic edit. Splitting a method, renaming a class or rewriting a section is not, so those findings remain until someone edits the code or the document.

Each message names the offending file and symbol, what the policy expects, and how to comply. It also says that changing the declaration itself needs a human to update `guard.yaml`, so an agent fixes the project instead of the policy.

## Workflow

1. Run `guard init` to write a `guard.yaml` that imports the presets matching the project. See [init](cli.md#init).
2. Review the file, adjust thresholds and declarations in the [configuration](configuration.md), and commit it.
3. Run `guard fix --dry-run`, then `guard fix`, to bring the tool configuration in line.
4. Fix the remaining findings in code and documents until `guard check` passes.
5. Run `guard check` in CI. When a finding reflects a deliberate decision, a human changes `guard.yaml` in the same change.

## What it does not prove

Guard checks shape: sizes, names, headings and values. A short method can still be wrong, and a README with the declared sections can still be out of date. Passing `guard check` means the project has not drifted from what was decided, not that the decisions are good.

1	# PHPStan Rules
2	
3	Custom PHPStan rules provided by php-ai-toolkit. Each rule detects anti-patterns that actually occur in AI-generated code.
4	
5	## Rector Support
6	
7	Every rule below is classified as **Safe**, **Risky**, or **Unavailable** for automatic
8	changes. Enable the safe group with `withRules(SafeRules::rules())` or the risky
9	group with `withRules(RiskyRules::rules())` in `rector.php`. Both classes are in
10	`Toolkit\Rector`; their lists can be combined, and individual Rector classes can
11	also be registered with `withRules()`.
12	A classification describes only the supported cases; each rule’s Rector section
13	lists skipped cases and review requirements.
14	
15	The legacy opt-in [ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule](rules/ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule.md#rector)
16	is also classified as **Unavailable**. Internal helper rules for mixed types and
17	class dispatch share their parent rule’s classification.
18	
19	## General
20	
21	Rules applied to all code.
22	
23	| Rule | Description | Error Identifier | Rector |
24	|------|-------------|------------------|--------|
25	| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md) | Forbids `@phpstan-ignore` and `@infection-ignore-all` comments | `customRules.phpstanIgnoreComment`, `customRules.infectionIgnoreAllComment` | [Risky](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) |
26	| [ForbidFileTermRule](rules/ForbidFileTermRule.md) | Forbids configured literal terms in files matching restricted path patterns | `customRules.forbiddenFileTerm` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidFileTermRule.md#rector) |
27	| [ForbidDependencyRule](rules/ForbidDependencyRule.md) | Forbids symbol and file-reading dependencies between configured paths; allows each root directory to depend only on itself and src by default | `customRules.forbiddenDependency` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidDependencyRule.md#rector) |
28	| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md) | Forbids direct calls to magic methods | `customRules.forbiddenMagicMethodCall` | [Risky](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) |
29	| [ForbiddenNamespaceRule](rules/ForbiddenNamespaceRule.md) | Forbids configured namespace prefixes and whole segments at any depth, including `Model`, `Models`, `Infrastructure`, and `Infrastructures` by default | `customRules.forbiddenNamespace` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbiddenNamespaceRule.md#rector) |
30	| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md) | Requires `#[Override]` attribute on overridden methods | `customRules.overrideMustHaveAttribute` | [Safe](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) |
31	| [SrcUnitTestPairRule](rules/SrcUnitTestPairRule.md) | Enforces 1:1 pairing between `src/` classes and `tests/Unit/` test classes | `customRules.srcUnitTestPair` | [Unavailable](rules/SrcUnitTestPairRule.md#rector) |
32	| [RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule](rules/RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule.md) | Requires PHPDoc on all public API elements | `customRules.requirePhpDocOnPublicApi` | [Unavailable](rules/RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule.md#rector) |
33	| [RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule](rules/RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule.md) | Requires a runnable `@example` on declarations marked `@visibility public` | `customRules.requireExampleOnClass`, `customRules.requireExampleOnMethod`, `customRules.requireExampleOnProperty`, `customRules.requireExampleOnConstant`, `customRules.requireExampleOnEnumCase` | [Unavailable](rules/RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule.md#rector) |
34	| [EnforceVisibilityScopeRule](rules/EnforceVisibilityScopeRule.md) | Enforces namespace visibility scopes declared with `@visibility` and treats explicitly public API as externally used | `customRules.visibilityInvalidScope`, `customRules.visibilityOutOfScope` | [Unavailable](rules/EnforceVisibilityScopeRule.md#rector) |
35	| [EnforceMutationContractRule](rules/EnforceMutationContractRule.md) | Makes parameter, receiver, and global mutation explicit and propagates effects through statically resolved calls | `customRules.mutationInvalidContract`, `customRules.mutationUndeclared`, `customRules.mutationOverrideWidened` | [Unavailable](rules/EnforceMutationContractRule.md#rector) |
36	| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md) | Forbids `/* */` and `#` comments everywhere, and `//` comments outside `catch` blocks and array literals; `/** */` PHPDoc is allowed | `customRules.forbidNonDocComment` | [Risky](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) |
37	| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md) | Forbids single-line PHPDoc on public elements; requires multi-line format | `customRules.forbidSingleLinePhpDoc` | [Safe](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md#rector) |
38	| [ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule](rules/ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule.md) | Forbids configured suffixes on class, interface, trait, and enum names | `customRules.forbiddenClassLikeNameSuffix` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule.md#rector) |
39	| [NoNonPublicMethodRule](rules/NoNonPublicMethodRule.md) | Forbids private methods and forbids protected methods outside abstract classes, traits, and override methods; constructors are exempt | `customRules.nonPublicMethod` | [Unavailable](rules/NoNonPublicMethodRule.md#rector) |
40	| [ForbidEmptyCatchRule](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md) | Forbids catch blocks with an empty body | `customRules.emptyCatch` | [Risky](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md#rector) |
41	| [RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md) | Requires `@throws` for exceptions thrown directly in a method and not caught within it | `customRules.missingThrowsTag` | [Risky](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md#rector) |
42	| [RequireExceptionChainingRule](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md) | Requires new exceptions thrown inside catch blocks to chain the caught exception | `customRules.unchainedRethrow` | [Risky](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md#rector) |
43	| [ForbidBroadCatchRule](rules/ForbidBroadCatchRule.md) | Forbids catching `Throwable`, `Exception`, and the `LogicException`/`Error` families outside configured boundary paths | `customRules.broadCatch` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidBroadCatchRule.md#rector) |
44	| [ForbidGenericThrowsTagRule](rules/ForbidGenericThrowsTagRule.md) | Forbids `@throws \Exception` and `@throws \Throwable` tags | `customRules.genericThrowsTag` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidGenericThrowsTagRule.md#rector) |
45	| [ForbidInternalMixedTypeRule](rules/ForbidInternalMixedTypeRule.md) | Forbids explicit concrete `mixed` in internal declarations while allowing public, inherited, magic-protocol, and template contracts | `customRules.internalMixedType` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidInternalMixedTypeRule.md#rector) |
46	| [RequireListForArrayLiteralRule](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md) | Requires `list<V>` instead of `array<int, V>` when a property or callable visibly owns a non-empty list literal; input parameters remain unrestricted | `customRules.arrayLiteralListType` | [Risky](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md#rector) |
47	| [RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule](rules/RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule.md) | Requires a `switch` or `match` that names its subject — `match ($suit)`, or `match ($payment::class)` for a sealed hierarchy — to name a branch for every value that subject can hold, the way Rust and Kotlin check a match over a closed type | `customRules.exhaustiveDispatch`, `customRules.exhaustiveDispatchDefault` | [Unavailable](rules/RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule.md#rector) |
48	
49	## Test Class
50	
51	Rules applied to test classes in the `Tests\Unit` / `Tests\Integration` namespaces. Rules marked with `*` apply to all `Tests\` namespaces.
52	
53	| Rule | Description | Error Identifier | Rector |
54	|------|-------------|------------------|--------|
55	| [NoPropertyInTestClassRule](rules/NoPropertyInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids property declarations in test classes | `customRules.noPropertyInTestClass` | [Unavailable](rules/NoPropertyInTestClassRule.md#rector) |
56	| [NoClassConstantInTestClassRule](rules/NoClassConstantInTestClassRule.md) | Forbids class constants in test classes | `customRules.noClassConstantInTestClass` | [Unavailable](rules/NoClassConstantInTestClassRule.md#rector) |

67	
68	## Enabling and Disabling Rules
69	
70	Rules inherit `toolkit.allRules`, which defaults to `true`, except mutation
71	contracts, which are opt-in so an existing unannotated project does not change
72	semantics on upgrade. Override a specific rule through its `enabled` value:
73	
74	```neon
75	parameters:
76	    toolkit:
77	        forbidEmptyCatch:
78	            enabled: false
79	```
80	
81	Set `allRules: false` to make every rule opt-in. Toolkit adoption keeps the
82	default; changing a switch is an explicit project policy decision.
83	
84	Enable mutation contracts explicitly with `toolkit.mutation.enabled: true`.
85	
86	## Redundant PHPStan Diagnostics
87	
88	The toolkit suppresses a PHPStan or Strict Rules diagnostic only when an enabled
89	toolkit rule makes that diagnostic non-actionable. The toolkit error remains as
90	the single instruction for fixing the prohibited construct:
91	
92	| Enabled toolkit rule | Suppressed diagnostic | Scope |
93	|----------------------|-----------------------|-------|
94	| `noNonPublicMethod` | `method.unused`, `method.finalPrivate` | Private method declarations; PHPStan does not emit either for constructors, and `consistentConstructor.private` stays visible because the rule exempts constructors |
95	| `noPrivateMethodInTestClass` | The same private-method diagnostics | Restricted test classes |
96	| `noPropertyInTestClass` | `property.unused`, `property.neverRead`, `property.neverWritten`, `property.onlyRead`, `property.onlyWritten` | Restricted test classes |
97	| `noClassConstantInTestClass` | `classConstant.unused` | Restricted test classes |
98	| `noControlFlowInTestMethod` | PHPStan and Strict Rules diagnostics emitted for the prohibited `if`, loop, `switch`, or `match` node | Test methods in restricted test classes |
99	| `requireThrowsTagOnDirectThrow` | `missingType.checkedException` | Direct escaping throws in methods; propagated checked exceptions remain reported |
100	
101	This is semantic suppression through PHPStan's extension API, not a global
102	`ignoreErrors` entry. Disabling the dominating toolkit rule automatically
103	restores the corresponding PHPStan diagnostics. Independent findings remain
104	visible; for example, an unused private property in production code and a dead
105	broad catch are still reported.
106	
107	## Parameters
108	
109	The following values can be customized under `parameters.toolkit` in a project's
110	`phpstan.neon`:
111	
112	| Parameter | Default | Description |
113	|-----------|---------|-------------|
114	| `testNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests']` | Test namespace prefixes |
115	| `restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests\Unit', 'Tests\Integration']` | Test namespaces where strict rules apply |
116	| `visibilityExemptNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests']` | Namespace subtrees allowed to reference declarations across `@visibility` boundaries |
117	| `srcUnitTestPairExcludePatterns` | `[]` | Patterns to exclude from test pair checks |
118	| `srcMarker` | `'/src/'` | Source code path marker |
119	| `unitTestMarker` | `'/tests/Unit/'` | Unit test path marker |
120	| `forbiddenTermsByPath` | `[]` | Map of restricted file path patterns to case-insensitive literal terms forbidden anywhere in matching files |
121	| `dependencyProjectRoot` | `%currentWorkingDirectory%` | Absolute root for dependency boundary patterns |
122	| `forbiddenDependencies` | Root directories may depend on themselves and `src/**`; `vendor/**` and root files are exempt | Directed `from`/`to` path policies with optional `excludeFrom`, `excludeTo`, and `allowSameRootDirectory` |
123	| `dependencyFileReaders` | `[]` | Additional function or `Class::method` file readers with argument `position` and `name`; built-ins remain active |
124	| `forbiddenNamespacePrefixes` | `['Tests\Support', 'Tests\Supports', 'Tests\Helper', 'Tests\Helpers', 'Tests\Util', 'Tests\Utils', 'Tests\Utility', 'Tests\Utilities', 'Tests\Fixture', 'Tests\Fixtures']` | Namespace prefixes to forbid |
125	| `forbiddenNamespaceSegments` | `['Model', 'Models', 'Infrastructure', 'Infrastructures']` | Whole namespace segments to forbid at any depth; matching is case-sensitive |
126	| `forbiddenClassLikeNameSuffixes` | See [`rules.neon`](../rules.neon) | Class-like declaration name suffixes to forbid |
127	| `broadCatchAllowedPaths` | `[]` | fnmatch patterns of boundary files allowed to catch `Throwable`, `Exception`, and the `LogicException`/`Error` families |
128

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	package="${1:?Usage: prepare-package.sh PACKAGE OUTPUT [vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH]}"
5	output="${2:?Pass an empty output directory.}"
6	tag="${3:-}"
7	root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
8	cd "$root"
9	
10	if [[ ! "$package" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]+$ ]] || [ ! -f "packages/$package/composer.json" ]; then
11	  echo "Unknown package '$package'; choose a directory in packages/." >&2
12	  exit 1
13	fi
14	if [ -n "$tag" ] && [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$ ]]; then
15	  echo "Invalid release tag '$tag'; use vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, for example v0.1.0." >&2
16	  exit 1

21	  exit 1
22	fi

24	# Export committed files only: never copy local vendor/, caches or build output.
25	git archive "HEAD:packages/$package" | tar -x -C "$output"
26	names="$(jq -s 'map(.name)' packages/*/composer.json)"
27	constraint=dev-main
28	if [ -n "$tag" ]; then
29	  constraint="^${tag#v}"
30	fi
31	jq --argjson names "$names" --arg constraint "$constraint" --arg package "$package" '
32	  del(.repositories, .version) |
33	  .homepage = "https://k-kinzal.github.io/php-ai-toolkit/" |
34	  .support = ((.support // {}) + {
35	    source: ("https://github.com/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/tree/main/packages/" + $package),
36	    issues: "https://github.com/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/issues",
37	    docs: "https://k-kinzal.github.io/php-ai-toolkit/"
38	  }) |
39	  (.require, ."require-dev") |= with_entries(
40	    if (.key as $name | $names | index($name)) != null
41	    then .value = $constraint else . end
42	  )
43	' "$output/composer.json" > "$output/composer.json.tmp"
44	mv "$output/composer.json.tmp" "$output/composer.json"
45	rm -f "$output"/composer.lock "$output"/composer.lock.php-*
46	
47	# Composer's GitHub dist archives should contain the runtime and documentation.
48	cat >> "$output/.gitattributes" <<'EOF'
49	/.gitattributes export-ignore
50	/.gitignore export-ignore
51	/.php-cs-fixer.dist.php export-ignore
52	/deptrac.yaml export-ignore
53	/guard.yaml export-ignore
54	/infection.json* export-ignore
55	/phpcs.xml* export-ignore
56	/phpstan.neon* export-ignore
57	/phpunit*.xml* export-ignore

2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
5	test_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
6	trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT
7	
8	# Use real Git archives as Composer dist packages, including export-ignore rules.
9	# Both release and dev dependencies must resolve without the monorepo path repos.
10	for version in dev-main 0.1.0; do
11	  stage="$test_dir/$version"
12	  mkdir -p "$stage/consumer"
13	  definitions="$stage/packages.jsonl"
14	  tag=''
15	  if [ "$version" != dev-main ]; then
16	    tag="v$version"
17	  fi
18	  for manifest in "$root"/packages/*/composer.json; do
19	    package="$(basename "$(dirname "$manifest")")"
20	    output="$stage/$package"
21	    bash "$root/.github/scripts/prepare-package.sh" "$package" "$output" "$tag"
22	    git -C "$output" init --quiet --initial-branch=main
23	    git -C "$output" add --all
24	    git -C "$output" -c user.name=Test -c user.email=test@example.com commit --quiet -m Package
25	    git -C "$output" archive --format=zip --output="$stage/$package.zip" HEAD
26	    jq --arg version "$version" --arg url "$stage/$package.zip" '
27	      . + {version: $version, dist: {type: "zip", url: $url}}
28	    ' "$output/composer.json" >> "$definitions"
29	  done
30	  jq -s --arg version "$version" '{
31	    name: "test/split-consumer",
32	    require: (map({key: .name, value: $version}) | from_entries),
33	    repositories: [{type: "package", package: .}],
34	    config: {"allow-plugins": false}
35	  }' "$definitions" > "$stage/consumer/composer.json"
36	  composer update --working-dir="$stage/consumer" --no-interaction --no-plugins --no-scripts --prefer-dist
37	  composer check-platform-reqs --working-dir="$stage/consumer"
38	  "$stage/consumer/vendor/bin/guard" --help >/dev/null
39	  "$stage/consumer/vendor/bin/docgen" --help >/dev/null
40	  cat > "$stage/consumer/phpstan.neon" <<'EOF'
41	includes:
42	    - vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rules.neon
43	    - vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-ai-formatter/extension.neon
44	parameters:
45	    level: 1
46	    paths:
47	        - smoke.php
48	    toolkit:
49	        allRules: false
50	EOF
51	  printf '<?php\ndeclare(strict_types=1);\necho "Package smoke test";\n' > "$stage/consumer/smoke.php"
52	  "$stage/consumer/vendor/bin/phpstan" analyse --configuration="$stage/consumer/phpstan.neon" --no-progress
53	  php -r '
54	    require $argv[1] . "/vendor/autoload.php";
55	    foreach (glob($argv[1] . "/vendor/k-kinzal/*/composer.json") as $file) {
56	        $manifest = json_decode(file_get_contents($file), true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
57	        if (isset($manifest["repositories"]) || is_file(dirname($file) . "/composer.lock")) {
58	            throw new RuntimeException("Monorepo development configuration leaked into " . $file);
59	        }
60	        if (is_dir(dirname($file) . "/tests") || !is_file(dirname($file) . "/LICENSE")) {
61	            throw new RuntimeException("Incorrect distribution contents in " . $file);
62	        }
63	    }
64	  ' "$stage/consumer"
65	done
66	
67	# Exercise actual pushes locally: updates, unchanged reruns, immutable releases,
68	# and releasing an older snapshot without rolling main back.
69	git init --quiet --bare --initial-branch=main "$test_dir/remote.git"
70	git clone --quiet "$test_dir/remote.git" "$test_dir/mirror"
71	git -C "$test_dir/mirror" -c user.name=Test -c user.email=test@example.com commit --quiet --allow-empty -m Initialize
72	git -C "$test_dir/mirror" push --quiet origin main
73	snapshot="$test_dir/dev-main/docgen-php"
74	rm -rf "$snapshot/.git"
75	bash "$root/.github/scripts/push-package.sh" "$snapshot" "$test_dir/mirror" first
76	first="$(git -C "$test_dir/mirror" rev-parse HEAD)"
77	bash "$root/.github/scripts/push-package.sh" "$snapshot" "$test_dir/mirror" first
78	test "$first" = "$(git -C "$test_dir/mirror" rev-parse HEAD)"
79	echo 'Newer main snapshot' >> "$snapshot/README.md"
80	bash "$root/.github/scripts/push-package.sh" "$snapshot" "$test_dir/mirror" second
81	main="$(git -C "$test_dir/mirror" rev-parse HEAD)"
82	release="$test_dir/0.1.0/docgen-php"
83	rm -rf "$release/.git"
84	bash "$root/.github/scripts/push-package.sh" "$release" "$test_dir/mirror" first v0.1.0
85	bash "$root/.github/scripts/push-package.sh" "$release" "$test_dir/mirror" first v0.1.0
86	test "$main" = "$(git --git-dir="$test_dir/remote.git" rev-parse main)"
87	echo 'Conflicting release' >> "$release/README.md"
88	if bash "$root/.github/scripts/push-package.sh" "$release" "$test_dir/mirror" first v0.1.0; then
89	  echo 'A published tag was unexpectedly replaced.' >&2
90	  exit 1
91	fi
92	echo 'Package installation and split push checks passed.'

1	# Policies
2	
3	An AI agent that is asked to make a test pass will also lengthen a method, add a `Helper` class, open a new section in the README or lower the PHPStan level, if nothing stops it. Each of those changes looks reasonable alone. Guard declares what the project has decided about them in `guard.yaml`, reports every change that departs from it, and repairs the departures that have exactly one correct fix.
4	
5	## Policies
6	
7	| Section | What it checks | Rule IDs | Repaired by `fix` |
8	|---------|----------------|----------|---------------------|
9	| `metrics` | Lines and cyclomatic complexity of PHP files, classes, functions and methods. See [metrics](metrics.md). | `metrics.*` | no |
10	| `structure` | What each directory may contain, how entries are named, and how many there are. See [structure](structure.md). | `structure.*` | no |
11	| `documentation` | The headings, outline, badges or exact content of Markdown files, and Markdown files nobody declared. See [documents](documents.md). | `documentation.*` | no |
12	| `configuration` | Values in the configuration files of other tools, such as `phpstan.neon` or `phpunit.xml.dist`. See [configuration fields](fields.md). | the rule's `id` | yes, when the rule has a repair |
13	| `extensions` | Whatever a project or a package adds. See [extensions](extensions.md). | chosen by the extension | when the extension proposes a change |
14	
15	A section that `guard.yaml` neither writes nor [imports](configuration.md#imports) is not checked.
16	
17	## Required and recommended
18	
19	Every finding is either required or recommended. A required finding is reported as `error` and fails the command with exit code `1`. A recommendation is reported as `warning` and leaves the exit code at `0`. Configuration rules choose their level with `level`; metric, structure and document findings are always required.
20	
21	## What is repaired
22	
23	`guard fix` only writes configuration fields. A field has one value that satisfies its rule, or a declared fallback, so writing it is a deterministic edit. Splitting a method, renaming a class or rewriting a section is not, so those findings remain until someone edits the code or the document.
24	
25	Each message names the offending file and symbol, what the policy expects, and how to comply. It also says that changing the declaration itself needs a human to update `guard.yaml`, so an agent fixes the project instead of the policy.
26	
27	## Workflow
28	
29	1. Run `guard init` to write a `guard.yaml` that imports the presets matching the project. See [init](cli.md#init).
30	2. Review the file, adjust thresholds and declarations in the [configuration](configuration.md), and commit it.
31	3. Run `guard fix --dry-run`, then `guard fix`, to bring the tool configuration in line.
32	4. Fix the remaining findings in code and documents until `guard check` passes.
33	5. Run `guard check` in CI. When a finding reflects a deliberate decision, a human changes `guard.yaml` in the same change.
34	
35	## What it does not prove
36	
37	Guard checks shape: sizes, names, headings and values. A short method can still be wrong, and a README with the declared sections can still be out of date. Passing `guard check` means the project has not drifted from what was decided, not that the decisions are good.
38

1	# RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule
2	
3	| Property | Value |
4	|----------|-------|
5	| Identifier | `customRules.exhaustiveDispatch`, `customRules.exhaustiveDispatchDefault` |
6	| Scope | Every `switch` statement and every `match` expression |
7	| Rector | Unavailable |
8	| Rule classes | `RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule`, `RequireExhaustiveClassDispatchRule` |
9	| Configurable | No |
10	
11	## What It Detects
12	
13	Rust, Kotlin, and Swift refuse to compile a `match`/`when`/`switch` that leaves a variant of a
14	closed type out. That refusal is the point: adding a variant makes the compiler list every place
15	that has to be looked at again. PHP has no such check, and `default` removes even the runtime
16	`UnhandledMatchError`, so a case added to an enum today reaches `default` everywhere tomorrow and
17	the program keeps running with the wrong answer.
18	
19	This rule reads the closed set of values out of the subject's own type, so nothing has to be
20	annotated:
21	
22	```php
23	enum Suit: string
24	{
25	    case Hearts = 'hearts';
26	    case Diamonds = 'diamonds';
27	    case Spades = 'spades';
28	    case Clubs = 'clubs';
29	}
30	
31	// ERROR: Match expression sends Suit::Spades, Suit::Clubs to its "default" arm. Write an arm for
32	// each of those values so that a value added to the closed type is reported here instead of
33	// silently taking "default".
34	$colour = match ($suit) {
35	    Suit::Hearts, Suit::Diamonds => 'red',
36	    default => 'black',
37	};
38	
39	// ERROR: Switch statement does not handle Suit::Spades, Suit::Clubs. Write a "case" for each of
40	// those values: the subject holds a closed set of values and this switch has no "default", so
41	// those fall through it unhandled.
42	switch ($suit) {
43	    case Suit::Hearts:
44	        return 'red';
45	    case Suit::Diamonds:
46	        return 'red';
47	}
48	```
49	
50	### Which subjects are closed
51	
52	A subject is closed when PHP itself bounds the values it admits. The rule asks the analyzer for
53	that list; where there is none, the dispatch is left alone.
54	
55	| Subject type | Values |
56	|--------------|--------|
57	| An enum | its cases |
58	| `bool` | `true` and `false` |
59	| A union of literals, e.g. `'fast'\|'safe'\|'dry'` or a `@param self::MODE_*` tag | those literals |
60	| A nullable closed type, e.g. `?Suit` | `null` plus the cases |
61	| `$shape::class` or `get_class($shape)` | every instantiable class the subject can be, including those below an interface or an abstract class, read out of the analysed code |
62	| `$suit->value` on a backed enum | the case values |
63	| Anything narrowed to fewer values earlier in the method | only what is left |
64	| `string`, `int`, `object`, an object subject that is not read through its class name | *(open — not reported)* |
65	| Any subject of a `match (true)` or `switch (true)` | *(the construct names no subject — not reported)* |
66	
67	### Which constructs state a subject
68	
69	Exhaustiveness can only be asked of a construct that says what it is answering for, and PHP has
70	two ways of saying it.
71	
72	The first is the subject written next to the keyword — `match ($suit)`, `switch ($mode)` — where
73	the values to cover are the values of that subject's type.
74	
75	The second is the class name of an object read in the subject: `match ($shape::class)` and
76	`switch (get_class($shape))`. The object is named, so the classes to cover follow from its type,
77	and a branch of such a table can hold nothing but a class name, so nothing unrelated can enter it.
78	This is the form a sealed hierarchy needs, and it works for an interface or an abstract class as
79	well as for a union:
80	
81	```php
82	interface Payment {}
83	final class Visa implements Payment {}
84	final class MasterCard implements Payment {}
85	final class BankTransfer implements Payment {}
86	
87	// ERROR: Match expression sends BankTransfer to its "default" arm. Write an arm for each of
88	// those values so that a value added to the closed type is reported here instead of silently
89	// taking "default".
90	return match ($payment::class) {
91	    Visa::class => $this->card($payment),
92	    MasterCard::class => $this->card($payment),
93	    default => throw new LogicException('unreachable'),
94	};
95	```
96	
97	Adding a fourth implementation of `Payment` anywhere in the project now fails analysis at this
98	line, which is the guarantee Kotlin gets from `sealed class` and Java from `sealed interface`.
99	
100	Two things follow from where that class list comes from:
101	
102	- The classes are gathered from the analysed paths, so the hierarchy is closed within them and
103	  nothing is claimed about code outside. That is the same boundary Kotlin draws (same module) and
104	  Java draws (same module, `permits` aside): a downstream implementation is invisible, and this
105	  check does not pretend otherwise.
106	- Because a class list is only complete once every file has been read, these errors are produced
107	  after the analysis rather than while the file is being read. They carry their file and line the
108	  same way, so `ignoreErrors` and editor navigation are unaffected.
109	
110	### Why `match (true)` is never read
111	
112	`match (true)` and `switch (true)` state no subject. The subject is a constant and every branch
113	carries a condition of its own, so an arm may test anything at all:
114	
115	```php
116	match (true) {
117	    $shape instanceof Circle => $this->circle($shape),
118	    $size > 10 => $this->chunked($shape),    // nothing says this table is about $shape
119	    default => $this->generic($shape),
120	}
121	```
122	
123	Nothing in the construct says the table is answering for `$shape` rather than for `$size`, or for
124	anything else an arm might reach. A set of values cannot be demanded of it, and that holds whether
125	`$shape` is typed as an interface or as `Circle|Square|Triangle`: the union says what `$shape` can
126	be, not what the table is for. Where the intent is a total dispatch, `$shape::class` says so.
127	
128	### The two identifiers
129	
130	| Identifier | Reported when |
131	|------------|---------------|
132	| `customRules.exhaustiveDispatch` | A `switch` names no `case` for a value and has no `default` either, so the value falls through the statement. |
133	| `customRules.exhaustiveDispatchDefault` | A `switch` or `match` has a `default` branch that absorbs values of the closed type. This is the check that makes adding a value break the build. |
134	
135	### Not reported
136	
137	- A `match` without a `default` arm. PHPStan already reports the values it leaves out under
138	  `match.unhandled`, and a second error on the same line would only duplicate it. A `switch` gets
139	  no such error from PHPStan, which is why this rule reports one.
140	- A dispatch that claims none of the values. That is a comparison which happens to sit on a closed
141	  type, not a half-finished dispatch — `if`-style code and single-branch `switch (true)` filters
142	  stay quiet.
143	- Any `match (true)` or `switch (true)`, for the reason above — including one whose branches all
144	  narrow the same expression. Write `$shape::class` where the table is meant to be total.
145	- A class-name dispatch whose branches are not all class names. One arm comparing against a plain
146	  string means the table is not answering for a set of classes, so nothing is required of it.
147	- A class-name dispatch that names no class of the subject's hierarchy at all. Like the
148	  claims-nothing case above, that is a comparison rather than a table.
149	- A subject that computes a class name rather than reading one, such as
150	  `match ($p === null ? Visa::class : $p::class)`. Only `$x::class` and `get_class($x)` name the
151	  object the table is answering for; anything else is a string whose values are unknown.
152	- A subject with more than 32 values. Past that the list stops being something a reader can act on,
153	  and the type is almost certainly not a hand-written set of alternatives.
154	
155	## Why This Is an Error
156	
157	1. **A closed type is a promise the dispatch has to keep**: An enum exists to say "one of exactly
158	   these". Every `default` over one turns that promise back into "anything", one call site at a
159	   time, and the analyzer stops being able to tell you where the next case has to be handled.
160	
161	2. **Adding a case has to break the build, not the behaviour**: This is the whole value of an
162	   exhaustive `match` in Rust or Kotlin. With a `default` arm, adding `Suit::Joker` compiles, ships,
163	   and silently takes the `'black'` branch. With every arm written out, the analyzer names the four
164	   files to open.
165	
166	3. **AI agents add enum cases**: Asked to support a new status, a model adds the case and updates
167	   the one dispatch it was looking at. `default => throw new LogicException('unreachable')` reads as
168	   defensive care and hides the other five dispatch sites — including the ones that quietly return a
169	   wrong value rather than throwing.
170	
171	4. **`switch` has no analyzer backstop at all**: PHPStan reports an unhandled `match`; it reports
172	   nothing for a `switch`. A `switch` over an enum that misses a case falls straight through and the
173	   method returns `null` or continues with a stale variable.
174	
175	## How to Fix
176	
177	### Write the missing branches
178	
179	```php
180	$colour = match ($suit) {
181	    Suit::Hearts, Suit::Diamonds => 'red',
182	    Suit::Spades, Suit::Clubs => 'black',
183	};
184	```
185	
186	With every case named, the `default` arm is no longer needed at all: PHPStan proves the `match`
187	exhaustive and stops asking for one. Adding `Suit::Joker` then fails analysis at this line.
188	
189	### Keep the default where the analyzer still wants one
190	
191	A class-name dispatch cannot be proven exhaustive by PHPStan — it only knows the subject is some
192	`class-string<Payment>` — so it needs a `default` arm to satisfy `match.unhandled`. That is fine:
193	this rule reports only the classes that arm actually absorbs, so once every class has its own arm
194	the `default` is a formality and both checks are satisfied.
195	
196	```php
197	return match ($payment::class) {
198	    Visa::class => $this->card($payment),
199	    MasterCard::class => $this->card($payment),
200	    BankTransfer::class => $this->transfer($payment),
201	    default => throw new LogicException('unreachable'),
202	};
203	```
204	
205	### Say which type the table is answering for
206	
207	`match (true)` states nothing about its subject, so a hierarchy dispatch written that way is not
208	checked. Read the class name instead, which names the object:
209	
210	```php
211	-return match (true) {
212	-    $shape instanceof Circle => $shape->area(),
213	-    $shape instanceof Square => $shape->area(),
214	+return match ($shape::class) {
215	+    Circle::class => $shape->area(),
216	+    Square::class => $shape->area(),
217	     default => throw new LogicException('unreachable'),
218	 };
219	```
220	
221	Note that `case Circle::class` matches `Circle` and not a subclass of it, so a class-name dispatch
222	treats every instantiable subclass as its own value to answer for. That is exact rather than
223	strict: it is what the comparison actually does at runtime.
224	
225	### Turn the hierarchy into an enum
226	
227	Where the classes carry no state of their own, an enum is the closed type PHP does have, and every
228	dispatch over it is checked without any further work.
229	
230	### Suppress one of the two checks
231	
232	The catch-all check is the stricter half. A project that wants unhandled `switch` values reported
233	but accepts `default` branches can keep the first and drop the second:
234	
235	```neon
236	parameters:
237	    ignoreErrors:
238	        - identifier: customRules.exhaustiveDispatchDefault
239	```
240	
241	## Rector
242	
243	**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.
244	
245	Each missing enum, literal, or sealed-class branch needs a meaningful result. Inventing a throw/default branch can discard business behavior; removing a default may change future or out-of-contract behavior. This also covers the internal `RequireExhaustiveClassDispatchRule` implementation.
246
