1	# RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule
2	
3	| Property | Value |
4	|----------|-------|
5	| Identifier | `customRules.exhaustiveDispatch`, `customRules.exhaustiveDispatchDefault` |
6	| Scope | Every `switch` statement and every `match` expression |
7	| Rector | Unavailable |
8	| Rule classes | `RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule`, `RequireExhaustiveClassDispatchRule` |
9	| Configurable | No |
10	
11	## What It Detects
12	
13	Rust, Kotlin, and Swift refuse to compile a `match`/`when`/`switch` that leaves a variant of a
14	closed type out. That refusal is the point: adding a variant makes the compiler list every place
15	that has to be looked at again. PHP has no such check, and `default` removes even the runtime
16	`UnhandledMatchError`, so a case added to an enum today reaches `default` everywhere tomorrow and
17	the program keeps running with the wrong answer.
18	
19	This rule reads the closed set of values out of the subject's own type, so nothing has to be
20	annotated:
21	
22	```php
23	enum Suit: string
24	{
25	    case Hearts = 'hearts';
26	    case Diamonds = 'diamonds';
27	    case Spades = 'spades';
28	    case Clubs = 'clubs';
29	}
30	
31	// ERROR: Match expression sends Suit::Spades, Suit::Clubs to its "default" arm. Write an arm for
32	// each of those values so that a value added to the closed type is reported here instead of
33	// silently taking "default".
34	$colour = match ($suit) {
35	    Suit::Hearts, Suit::Diamonds => 'red',
36	    default => 'black',
37	};
38	
39	// ERROR: Switch statement does not handle Suit::Spades, Suit::Clubs. Write a "case" for each of
40	// those values: the subject holds a closed set of values and this switch has no "default", so
41	// those fall through it unhandled.
42	switch ($suit) {
43	    case Suit::Hearts:
44	        return 'red';
45	    case Suit::Diamonds:
46	        return 'red';
47	}
48	```
49	
50	### Which subjects are closed
51	
52	A subject is closed when PHP itself bounds the values it admits. The rule asks the analyzer for
53	that list; where there is none, the dispatch is left alone.
54	
55	| Subject type | Values |
56	|--------------|--------|
57	| An enum | its cases |
58	| `bool` | `true` and `false` |
59	| A union of literals, e.g. `'fast'\|'safe'\|'dry'` or a `@param self::MODE_*` tag | those literals |
60	| A nullable closed type, e.g. `?Suit` | `null` plus the cases |
61	| `$shape::class` or `get_class($shape)` | every instantiable class the subject can be, including those below an interface or an abstract class, read out of the analysed code |
62	| `$suit->value` on a backed enum | the case values |
63	| Anything narrowed to fewer values earlier in the method | only what is left |
64	| `string`, `int`, `object`, an object subject that is not read through its class name | *(open — not reported)* |
65	| Any subject of a `match (true)` or `switch (true)` | *(the construct names no subject — not reported)* |
66	
67	### Which constructs state a subject
68	
69	Exhaustiveness can only be asked of a construct that says what it is answering for, and PHP has
70	two ways of saying it.
71	
72	The first is the subject written next to the keyword — `match ($suit)`, `switch ($mode)` — where
73	the values to cover are the values of that subject's type.
74	
75	The second is the class name of an object read in the subject: `match ($shape::class)` and
76	`switch (get_class($shape))`. The object is named, so the classes to cover follow from its type,
77	and a branch of such a table can hold nothing but a class name, so nothing unrelated can enter it.
78	This is the form a sealed hierarchy needs, and it works for an interface or an abstract class as
79	well as for a union:
80	
81	```php
82	interface Payment {}
83	final class Visa implements Payment {}
84	final class MasterCard implements Payment {}
85	final class BankTransfer implements Payment {}
86	
87	// ERROR: Match expression sends BankTransfer to its "default" arm. Write an arm for each of
88	// those values so that a value added to the closed type is reported here instead of silently
89	// taking "default".
90	return match ($payment::class) {
91	    Visa::class => $this->card($payment),
92	    MasterCard::class => $this->card($payment),
93	    default => throw new LogicException('unreachable'),
94	};
95	```
96	
97	Adding a fourth implementation of `Payment` anywhere in the project now fails analysis at this
98	line, which is the guarantee Kotlin gets from `sealed class` and Java from `sealed interface`.
99	
100	Two things follow from where that class list comes from:
101	
102	- The classes are gathered from the analysed paths, so the hierarchy is closed within them and
103	  nothing is claimed about code outside. That is the same boundary Kotlin draws (same module) and
104	  Java draws (same module, `permits` aside): a downstream implementation is invisible, and this
105	  check does not pretend otherwise.
106	- Because a class list is only complete once every file has been read, these errors are produced
107	  after the analysis rather than while the file is being read. They carry their file and line the
108	  same way, so `ignoreErrors` and editor navigation are unaffected.
109	
110	### Why `match (true)` is never read
111	
112	`match (true)` and `switch (true)` state no subject. The subject is a constant and every branch
113	carries a condition of its own, so an arm may test anything at all:
114	
115	```php
116	match (true) {
117	    $shape instanceof Circle => $this->circle($shape),
118	    $size > 10 => $this->chunked($shape),    // nothing says this table is about $shape
119	    default => $this->generic($shape),
120	}
121	```
122	
123	Nothing in the construct says the table is answering for `$shape` rather than for `$size`, or for
124	anything else an arm might reach. A set of values cannot be demanded of it, and that holds whether
125	`$shape` is typed as an interface or as `Circle|Square|Triangle`: the union says what `$shape` can
126	be, not what the table is for. Where the intent is a total dispatch, `$shape::class` says so.
127	
128	### The two identifiers
129	
130	| Identifier | Reported when |
131	|------------|---------------|
132	| `customRules.exhaustiveDispatch` | A `switch` names no `case` for a value and has no `default` either, so the value falls through the statement. |
133	| `customRules.exhaustiveDispatchDefault` | A `switch` or `match` has a `default` branch that absorbs values of the closed type. This is the check that makes adding a value break the build. |
134	
135	### Not reported
136	
137	- A `match` without a `default` arm. PHPStan already reports the values it leaves out under
138	  `match.unhandled`, and a second error on the same line would only duplicate it. A `switch` gets
139	  no such error from PHPStan, which is why this rule reports one.
140	- A dispatch that claims none of the values. That is a comparison which happens to sit on a closed
141	  type, not a half-finished dispatch — `if`-style code and single-branch `switch (true)` filters
142	  stay quiet.
143	- Any `match (true)` or `switch (true)`, for the reason above — including one whose branches all
144	  narrow the same expression. Write `$shape::class` where the table is meant to be total.
145	- A class-name dispatch whose branches are not all class names. One arm comparing against a plain
146	  string means the table is not answering for a set of classes, so nothing is required of it.
147	- A class-name dispatch that names no class of the subject's hierarchy at all. Like the
148	  claims-nothing case above, that is a comparison rather than a table.
149	- A subject that computes a class name rather than reading one, such as
150	  `match ($p === null ? Visa::class : $p::class)`. Only `$x::class` and `get_class($x)` name the
151	  object the table is answering for; anything else is a string whose values are unknown.
152	- A subject with more than 32 values. Past that the list stops being something a reader can act on,
153	  and the type is almost certainly not a hand-written set of alternatives.
154	
155	## Why This Is an Error
156	
157	1. **A closed type is a promise the dispatch has to keep**: An enum exists to say "one of exactly
158	   these". Every `default` over one turns that promise back into "anything", one call site at a
159	   time, and the analyzer stops being able to tell you where the next case has to be handled.
160	
161	2. **Adding a case has to break the build, not the behaviour**: This is the whole value of an
162	   exhaustive `match` in Rust or Kotlin. With a `default` arm, adding `Suit::Joker` compiles, ships,
163	   and silently takes the `'black'` branch. With every arm written out, the analyzer names the four
164	   files to open.
165	
166	3. **AI agents add enum cases**: Asked to support a new status, a model adds the case and updates
167	   the one dispatch it was looking at. `default => throw new LogicException('unreachable')` reads as
168	   defensive care and hides the other five dispatch sites — including the ones that quietly return a
169	   wrong value rather than throwing.
170	
171	4. **`switch` has no analyzer backstop at all**: PHPStan reports an unhandled `match`; it reports
172	   nothing for a `switch`. A `switch` over an enum that misses a case falls straight through and the
173	   method returns `null` or continues with a stale variable.
174	
175	## How to Fix
176	
177	### Write the missing branches
178	
179	```php
180	$colour = match ($suit) {
181	    Suit::Hearts, Suit::Diamonds => 'red',
182	    Suit::Spades, Suit::Clubs => 'black',
183	};
184	```
185	
186	With every case named, the `default` arm is no longer needed at all: PHPStan proves the `match`
187	exhaustive and stops asking for one. Adding `Suit::Joker` then fails analysis at this line.
188	
189	### Keep the default where the analyzer still wants one
190	
191	A class-name dispatch cannot be proven exhaustive by PHPStan — it only knows the subject is some
192	`class-string<Payment>` — so it needs a `default` arm to satisfy `match.unhandled`. That is fine:
193	this rule reports only the classes that arm actually absorbs, so once every class has its own arm
194	the `default` is a formality and both checks are satisfied.
195	
196	```php
197	return match ($payment::class) {
198	    Visa::class => $this->card($payment),
199	    MasterCard::class => $this->card($payment),
200	    BankTransfer::class => $this->transfer($payment),
201	    default => throw new LogicException('unreachable'),
202	};
203	```
204	
205	### Say which type the table is answering for
206	
207	`match (true)` states nothing about its subject, so a hierarchy dispatch written that way is not
208	checked. Read the class name instead, which names the object:
209	
210	```php
211	-return match (true) {
212	-    $shape instanceof Circle => $shape->area(),
213	-    $shape instanceof Square => $shape->area(),
214	+return match ($shape::class) {
215	+    Circle::class => $shape->area(),
216	+    Square::class => $shape->area(),
217	     default => throw new LogicException('unreachable'),
218	 };
219	```
220	
221	Note that `case Circle::class` matches `Circle` and not a subclass of it, so a class-name dispatch
222	treats every instantiable subclass as its own value to answer for. That is exact rather than
223	strict: it is what the comparison actually does at runtime.
224	
225	### Turn the hierarchy into an enum
226	
227	Where the classes carry no state of their own, an enum is the closed type PHP does have, and every
228	dispatch over it is checked without any further work.
229	
230	### Suppress one of the two checks
231	
232	The catch-all check is the stricter half. A project that wants unhandled `switch` values reported
233	but accepts `default` branches can keep the first and drop the second:
234	
235	```neon
236	parameters:
237	    ignoreErrors:
238	        - identifier: customRules.exhaustiveDispatchDefault
239	```
240	
241	## Rector
242	
243	**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.
244	
245	Each missing enum, literal, or sealed-class branch needs a meaningful result. Inventing a throw/default branch can discard business behavior; removing a default may change future or out-of-contract behavior. This also covers the internal `RequireExhaustiveClassDispatchRule` implementation.
246

1	# TestNamingConventionRule
2	
3	| Property | Value |
4	|----------|-------|
5	| Identifiers | `customRules.testMethodNamingConvention`, `customRules.providerNamingConvention`, `customRules.testMethodProhibitedConstructorDestructor`, `customRules.publicMethodWithoutTest` |
6	| Scope | Test classes in restricted namespaces; source classes in `src/` |
7	| Rector | Unavailable |
8	| Configurable | Yes (namespace prefixes, path markers) |
9	
10	## What It Detects
11	
12	This rule enforces naming conventions for test methods and data providers in restricted test classes, prohibits testing constructors/destructors directly, and ensures every public method in source classes has a corresponding test method.
13	
14	### 1. Test method naming (`customRules.testMethodNamingConvention`)
15	
16	Test methods starting with `test` must follow PascalCase after the prefix: `test[MethodName]` or `test[MethodName][Behavior]`.
17	
18	```php
19	// ERROR: The prefix "test" alone is not a valid name.
20	public function test(): void { ... }
21	
22	// ERROR: After the "test" prefix, the next character must be an uppercase letter.
23	public function testsomething(): void { ... }
24	
25	// ERROR: Same — underscore is not uppercase.
26	public function test_something(): void { ... }
27	
28	// OK
29	public function testSomething(): void { ... }
30	public function testUserCanLogin(): void { ... }
31	```
32	
33	### 2. Data provider naming (`customRules.providerNamingConvention`)
34	
35	Data provider methods starting with `provider` must follow PascalCase after the prefix: `provider[TestCaseName]`.
36	
37	```php
38	// ERROR: The prefix "provider" alone is not a valid name.
39	public static function provider(): array { ... }
40	
41	// ERROR: After the "provider" prefix, the next character must be an uppercase letter.
42	public static function providerdata(): array { ... }
43	
44	// ERROR: Same — underscore is not uppercase.
45	public static function provider_data(): array { ... }
46	
47	// OK
48	public static function providerValidEmails(): array { ... }
49	public static function providerUserData(): array { ... }
50	```
51	
52	### 3. Prohibited constructor/destructor tests (`customRules.testMethodProhibitedConstructorDestructor`)
53	
54	Test methods whose name after `test` starts with `Construct` or `Destruct` are prohibited:
55	
56	```php
57	// ERROR: Tests a constructor directly.
58	public function testConstruct(): void { ... }
59	public function testConstructor(): void { ... }
60	public function testConstructThrowsException(): void { ... }
61	
62	// ERROR: Tests a destructor directly.
63	public function testDestruct(): void { ... }
64	public function testDestructor(): void { ... }
65	public function testDestructorIsCalled(): void { ... }
66	
67	// OK — "Reconstruct" does not start with "Construct"
68	public function testReconstructData(): void { ... }
69	```
70	
71	### 4. Public method test coverage (`customRules.publicMethodWithoutTest`)
72	
73	Every public non-magic method in a source file (`src/`) must have at least one corresponding test method starting with `test[MethodName]` in the unit test file. Abstract methods, magic methods (`__construct`, `__toString`, etc.), and private/protected methods are excluded.
74	
75	```php
76	// src/Service/UserService.php
77	class UserService
78	{
79	    public function create(User $user): void { ... }
80	    public function findById(int $id): ?User { ... }
81	    public function __construct(private Repository $repo) {}
82	    private function validate(User $user): void { ... }
83	}
84	```
85	
86	```php
87	// tests/Unit/Service/UserServiceTest.php
88	class UserServiceTest extends TestCase
89	{
90	    public function testCreatePersistsUser(): void { ... }      // OK — covers create()
91	    // ERROR: Add a unit test method starting with testFindById() for public method findById().
92	}
93	```
94	
95	## Why This Is an Error
96	
97	### Inconsistent naming reduces readability
98	
99	When test methods use inconsistent casing (`testsomething`, `test_something`), it becomes harder to scan test files and understand what each test covers. PascalCase after the `test` prefix (`testSomething`) creates a consistent, readable pattern across the entire test suite.
100	
101	### Bare prefixes carry no information
102	
103	A method named `test()` or `provider()` gives no indication of what it tests or what data it provides. Every test method and data provider should have a descriptive suffix that communicates its purpose.
104	
105	### Constructor/destructor testing couples tests to implementation
106	
107	Constructors and destructors are implementation details. Testing them directly (`testConstructor`, `testConstruct`) couples the test to the object's lifecycle rather than its behavior. When the constructor signature changes, these tests break even though the object's public behavior may be unchanged.
108	
109	### Untested public methods are invisible risks
110	
111	If a public method has no corresponding test, its behavior is unverified. The `test[MethodName]` naming convention makes it easy to see which methods are tested and which are not. When a test method must start with the source method name, missing coverage becomes immediately apparent.
112	
113	### AI anti-pattern
114	
115	AI code generators frequently create `testConstructor()` methods that simply verify an object can be instantiated — a test with no behavioral value. They also produce snake_case test names (`test_it_works`) from Python conventions or bare `test()` methods as placeholders. They also tend to skip writing tests for methods they consider "simple". This rule catches these patterns early.
116	
117	## How to Fix
118	
119	### Rename to PascalCase
120	
121	```php
122	// Before
123	public function testsomething(): void { ... }
124	public function test_user_can_login(): void { ... }
125	
126	// After
127	public function testSomething(): void { ... }
128	public function testUserCanLogin(): void { ... }
129	```
130	
131	### Add descriptive suffixes
132	
133	```php
134	// Before
135	public function test(): void { ... }
136	public static function provider(): array { ... }
137	
138	// After
139	public function testUserIsCreated(): void { ... }
140	public static function providerValidEmails(): array { ... }
141	```
142	
143	### Replace constructor tests with behavioral tests
144	
145	```php
146	// Before — testing the constructor directly
147	public function testConstructor(): void
148	{
149	    $user = new User('Alice', 30);
150	    self::assertSame('Alice', $user->name());
151	    self::assertSame(30, $user->age());
152	}
153	
154	// After — testing the behavior that the constructor enables
155	public function testNameReturnsGivenName(): void
156	{
157	    $user = new User('Alice', 30);
158	    self::assertSame('Alice', $user->name());
159	}
160	
161	public function testAgeReturnsGivenAge(): void
162	{
163	    $user = new User('Alice', 30);
164	    self::assertSame(30, $user->age());
165	}
166	```
167	
168	### Add tests for uncovered public methods
169	
170	```php
171	// Before — findById() has no test
172	class UserServiceTest extends TestCase
173	{
174	    public function testCreatePersistsUser(): void { ... }
175	}
176	
177	// After — every public method has at least one test
178	class UserServiceTest extends TestCase
179	{
180	    public function testCreatePersistsUser(): void { ... }
181	
182	    public function testFindByIdReturnsUser(): void { ... }
183	
184	    public function testFindByIdReturnsNullWhenNotFound(): void { ... }
185	}
186	```
187	
188	## Configuration
189	
190	Customize which namespaces are considered restricted and which path markers identify source/test directories:
191	
192	```neon
193	parameters:
194	    toolkit:
195	        restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes:
196	            - 'Tests\Unit'
197	            - 'Tests\Integration'
198	        srcMarker: '/src/'
199	        unitTestMarker: '/tests/Unit/'
200	```
201	
202	## Rector
203	
204	**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.
205	
206	Method and provider names must describe the scenario, and references in annotations, attributes, configuration, and filters must remain consistent.
207

1	# PhpUnitMockApiRule
2	
3	| Property | Value |
4	|----------|-------|
5	| Identifiers | `customRules.testClassPhpUnitMockProhibitedApi`, `customRules.testClassPhpUnitMockRequiresInterface`, `customRules.testClassPhpUnitMockRequiresLiteralInterface`, `customRules.testClassPhpUnitMockProhibitedInstantiation` |
6	| Scope | All test classes (`Tests\` namespace) |
7	| Rector | Unavailable |
8	| Configurable | Yes (namespace prefixes) |
9	
10	## What It Detects
11	
12	This rule enforces interface-only mocking by restricting how PHPUnit's mock API is used.
13	
14	### 1. Prohibited mock APIs (`customRules.testClassPhpUnitMockProhibitedApi`)
15	
16	The following methods are always forbidden:
17	
18	- `getMockBuilder()`
19	- `createPartialMock()`
20	- `createTestProxy()`
21	- `getMockForAbstractClass()`
22	- `getMockForTrait()`
23	- `getMockFromWsdl()`
24	
25	```php
26	// ERROR: Use createMock(FooInterface::class) or createStub(FooInterface::class) instead of PHPUnit getMockBuilder().
27	$mock = $this->getMockBuilder(FooInterface::class)
28	    ->disableOriginalConstructor()
29	    ->getMock();
30	
31	// ERROR: Use createMock(FooInterface::class) or createStub(FooInterface::class) instead of PHPUnit createPartialMock().
32	$mock = $this->createPartialMock(ConcreteService::class, ['process']);
33	```
34	
35	### 2. Interface-only enforcement (`customRules.testClassPhpUnitMockRequiresInterface`)
36	
37	`createMock()`, `createStub()`, `createConfiguredMock()`, and `createConfiguredStub()` must target an interface:
38	
39	```php
40	// ERROR: Pass an interface class-string to PHPUnit createMock(); "App\Service\UserService" is not an interface.
41	$mock = $this->createMock(UserService::class);
42	
43	// ERROR: Pass an interface class-string to PHPUnit createStub(); "App\Repository\OrderRepository" is not an interface.
44	$stub = $this->createStub(OrderRepository::class);
45	
46	// OK
47	$mock = $this->createMock(UserServiceInterface::class);
48	$stub = $this->createStub(OrderRepositoryInterface::class);
49	```
50	
51	### 3. Literal class-string required (`customRules.testClassPhpUnitMockRequiresLiteralInterface`)
52	
53	The first argument must be a direct `::class` constant fetch, not a variable or string:
54	
55	```php
56	// ERROR: Pass an interface class-string literal to PHPUnit createMock(), e.g. DependencyInterface::class.
57	$mock = $this->createMock($className);
58	
59	// ERROR: also reported
60	$mock = $this->createMock('App\Service\FooInterface');
61	
62	// OK
63	$mock = $this->createMock(FooInterface::class);
64	```
65	
66	### 4. Prohibited direct instantiation (`customRules.testClassPhpUnitMockProhibitedInstantiation`)
67	
68	Direct instantiation of `MockBuilder` and `MockGenerator` is forbidden:
69	
70	```php
71	// ERROR: Use createMock(FooInterface::class) or createStub(FooInterface::class) instead of instantiating PHPUnit\Framework\MockObject\MockBuilder directly.
72	$builder = new MockBuilder($this, FooInterface::class);
73	```
74	
75	## Why This Is an Error
76	
77	### Concrete class mocking couples tests to implementations
78	
79	When you mock a concrete class, PHPUnit creates a subclass that overrides its methods. This means your test depends on the class's constructor signature, method visibility, and inheritance chain. Any refactoring of the concrete class can break tests that never intended to test that class.
80	
81	```php
82	// Fragile: breaks if UserService changes its constructor
83	$mock = $this->createMock(UserService::class);
84	
85	// Stable: only depends on the interface contract
86	$mock = $this->createMock(UserServiceInterface::class);
87	```
88	
89	### Partial mocks hide design problems
90	
91	`createPartialMock()` and `getMockBuilder()` allow mocking only some methods while keeping real implementations for others. This typically indicates the class has too many responsibilities. Instead of partially mocking, redesign the class to follow the Single Responsibility Principle.
92	
93	### Non-literal class strings prevent static verification
94	
95	When the mock target is a variable or string literal, PHPStan cannot verify at analysis time that the target is an interface. This defeats the purpose of the rule.
96	
97	### AI anti-pattern
98	
99	AI code generators frequently mock concrete classes because they copy the class name directly from the production code. They also tend to use `getMockBuilder()` chains because training data contains older PHPUnit patterns. This rule forces the cleaner, modern API.
100	
101	## How to Fix
102	
103	### Replace concrete class mocking with interface mocking
104	
105	If no interface exists, create one:
106	
107	```php
108	// Before
109	class UserService
110	{
111	    public function findById(int $id): ?User { ... }
112	}
113	
114	// Step 1: Extract interface
115	interface UserServiceInterface
116	{
117	    public function findById(int $id): ?User;
118	}
119	
120	class UserService implements UserServiceInterface { ... }
121	
122	// Step 2: Mock the interface
123	$mock = $this->createMock(UserServiceInterface::class);
124	```
125	
126	### Replace getMockBuilder with createMock/createStub
127	
128	```php
129	// Bad
130	$mock = $this->getMockBuilder(FooInterface::class)
131	    ->disableOriginalConstructor()
132	    ->getMock();
133	$mock->method('bar')->willReturn('baz');
134	
135	// Good
136	$mock = $this->createStub(FooInterface::class);
137	$mock->method('bar')->willReturn('baz');
138	```
139	
140	### Replace createPartialMock with proper design
141	
142	```php
143	// Bad: partial mock indicates mixed responsibilities
144	$service = $this->createPartialMock(ReportService::class, ['fetchData']);
145	$service->method('fetchData')->willReturn([...]);
146	$result = $service->generateReport();
147	
148	// Good: separate the responsibilities
149	$fetcher = $this->createStub(DataFetcherInterface::class);
150	$fetcher->method('fetchData')->willReturn([...]);
151	
152	$service = new ReportService($fetcher);
153	$result = $service->generateReport();
154	```
155	
156	### Use createMock vs createStub
157	
158	- **`createStub()`**: When you only need to control return values (no expectation on call count)
159	- **`createMock()`**: When you need to verify that methods are called with specific arguments
160	
161	```php
162	// Stub: only controls behavior
163	$repository = $this->createStub(UserRepositoryInterface::class);
164	$repository->method('findById')->willReturn(new User('Alice'));
165	
166	// Mock: also verifies interactions
167	$logger = $this->createMock(LoggerInterface::class);
168	$logger->expects(self::once())
169	    ->method('info')
170	    ->with('User created: Alice');
171	```
172	
173	## Configuration
174	
175	Customize which namespaces are considered test classes:
176	
177	```neon
178	parameters:
179	    toolkit:
180	        testNamespacePrefixes:
181	            - 'Tests'
182	```
183	
184	## Rector
185	
186	**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.
187	
188	Selecting an interface, real collaborator, mock, or stub depends on the test contract and expected interactions.
189

1	# ForbidInternalMixedTypeRule
2	
3	| Property | Value |
4	|----------|-------|
5	| Identifier | `customRules.internalMixedType` |
6	| Scope | Resolved PHPStan declarations outside unrestricted public or inherited contracts |
7	| Rector | Unavailable |
8	| Configurable | No |
9	
10	## What It Detects
11	
12	Reports explicit, concrete `mixed` in a declaration that is internal to the program. The check follows the resolved PHPStan type, so nested occurrences are included:
13	
14	```php
15	/**
16	 * @visibility namespace
17	 */
18	final class PayloadDecoder
19	{
20	    /** @var array{payload: mixed} */
21	    private array $payload; // ERROR
22	
23	    /**
24	     * @param list<array<string, mixed>> $rows
25	     */
26	    public function decode(array $rows): string // ERROR
27	    {
28	        // ...
29	    }
30	}
31	```
32	
33	The rule covers:
34	
35	- Parameters and returns on scope-restricted classes, methods, and functions.
36	- Private properties, including promoted properties, even when their constructor is public.
37	- Properties on a scope-restricted class.
38	- Closure and arrow-function signatures.
39	- Explicit local `@var`, `@phpstan-var`, and `@psalm-var` declarations.
40	- Restricted class-level `@property`, `@method`, `@phpstan-type`, and `@psalm-type` declarations.
41	- `mixed` nested inside arrays, lists, iterables, callables, unions, and array shapes.
42	
43	An omitted type remains PHPStan's implicit `mixed` and is handled by PHPStan's ordinary missing-type checks. This rule targets an explicit type decision that discards information.
44	
45	## Public Boundary
46	
47	Arbitrary values are valid at an unrestricted public boundary. The rule therefore permits `mixed` automatically when both the PHP API visibility and the effective `@visibility` scope expose the declaration:
48	
49	```php
50	final class Input
51	{
52	    public function normalize(mixed $value): string
53	    {
54	        if (!is_string($value)) {
55	            throw new InvalidArgumentException('Expected a string.');
56	        }
57	
58	        return $value;
59	    }
60	}
61	```
62	
63	No `@visibility` tag and `@visibility public` both mean unrestricted for this rule. Public and protected members are contract surfaces. A private member remains internal, and a member can never be wider than a scope-restricted class containing it.
64	
65	The public boundary is allowed to accept or return any deliberate `mixed` contract. The architectural expectation is that arbitrary input is validated there and that the internal declarations receiving the result use the narrowed type.
66	
67	## Inherited Contracts
68	
69	An implementation is allowed to declare `mixed` when the corresponding position is imposed by:
70	
71	- A parent method.
72	- An implemented interface method.
73	- An abstract method imported from a trait.
74	
75	The exception is position-specific. An interface parameter declared as `mixed` permits that implementation parameter; it does not permit an unrelated return type or another method owned by the implementation.
76	
77	```php
78	interface Decoder
79	{
80	    public function decode(mixed $value): string;
81	}
82	
83	/**
84	 * @visibility namespace
85	 */
86	final class JsonDecoder implements Decoder
87	{
88	    public function decode(mixed $value): string // allowed by Decoder
89	    {
90	        // validate and normalize
91	    }
92	
93	    public function remember(mixed $value): void // ERROR: no inherited contract
94	    {
95	    }
96	}
97	```
98	
99	This applies equally to vendor, built-in, and same-project public contracts.
100	
101	An ancestor parameter with no declared type is implicit `mixed`. Parameter
102	contravariance therefore requires an override to continue accepting every
103	value, so an explicit `mixed` in that child parameter is also allowed. This
104	includes implicit `mixed` nested in an inherited type such as an unparameterized
105	`array`.
106	
107	An omitted ancestor return type does not grant the same exception. Return types
108	are covariant, so the child can and should declare the narrower type it actually
109	returns unless the ancestor explicitly requires `mixed`.
110	
111	## PHP Magic Protocols
112	
113	Recognized PHP magic methods are language-defined protocol methods and their signatures are permitted on restricted classes. Arbitrary names beginning with `__` are not magic protocols. `__construct`, `__destruct`, and `__clone` continue through the ordinary visibility and inherited-contract checks because they do not impose an arbitrary-value signature by themselves.
114	
115	## Templates Are Not Mixed
116	
117	A template represents one type selected by a caller; it is not concrete `mixed`. Native PHP may need an untyped slot to carry it, but PHPStan still knows the slot as `T`:
118	
119	```php
120	/**
121	 * @template T
122	 * @visibility namespace
123	 */
124	final class Box
125	{
126	    /** @var T */
127	    private $value;
128	
129	    /** @param T $value */
130	    public function __construct($value)
131	    {
132	        $this->value = $value;
133	    }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	`TemplateMixedType` and template occurrences nested inside another type are consequently not reported.
138	
139	## How to Fix
140	
141	Choose the fix that describes the real boundary:
142	
143	1. Validate the arbitrary value at an unrestricted public method and pass a narrowed union, shape, DTO, or domain object inward.
144	2. If consumers genuinely need an arbitrary-value contract, expose it as a public interface and implement that contract internally.
145	3. If the declaration is generic rather than arbitrary, declare a template such as `T` and use `T` at every corresponding position.
146	4. If the value set is closed, replace `mixed` with the complete union or array shape.
147	
148	There is no path allowlist. Whether `mixed` is valid is a property of the type contract, not the file containing it.
149	
150	## Rector
151	
152	**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.
153	
154	Determine and validate the actual type or deliberately expose a public boundary. Deleting `mixed` or guessing a narrower type is not a repair.
155

1	# NoHelperMethodInTestClassRule
2	
3	| Property | Value |
4	|----------|-------|
5	| Identifier | `customRules.testClassNonOverrideMethod` |
6	| Scope | Test classes in restricted namespaces |
7	| Rector | Unavailable |
8	| Configurable | Yes (namespace prefixes) |
9	
10	## What It Detects
11	
12	Reports methods in test classes that are not:
13	
14	- **Test methods**: methods starting with `test` or annotated with `#[Test]`
15	- **Data providers**: methods starting with `provider`
16	- **Framework overrides**: methods that override a parent class method (abstract implementations or `#[Override]`-annotated overrides)
17	
18	```php
19	namespace Tests\Unit\Service;
20	
21	final class UserServiceTest extends TestCase
22	{
23	    public function testCreate(): void { ... }
24	
25	    public function providerInvalidEmails(): array { ... }
26	
27	    #[Override]
28	    protected function setUp(): void { ... }
29	
30	    // ERROR: Move method buildUser() out of Tests\Unit\Service\UserServiceTest or make it a test, data provider, or framework override.
31	    protected function buildUser(string $name = 'Alice'): User
32	    {
33	        return new User($name, 'alice@example.com', 30);
34	    }
35	
36	    // ERROR: Move method assertUserIsValid() out of Tests\Unit\Service\UserServiceTest or make it a test, data provider, or framework override.
37	    protected function assertUserIsValid(User $user): void
38	    {
39	        self::assertNotEmpty($user->name());
40	        self::assertNotEmpty($user->email());
41	    }
42	}
43	```
44	
45	## Why This Is an Error
46	
47	Test classes should have a flat, predictable structure: test methods, data providers, and framework lifecycle overrides. Any other method is a helper that introduces problems:
48	
49	1. **Shared abstractions reduce readability**: A test should be a self-contained specification. When setup or assertions are hidden behind helper methods, the reader must navigate multiple methods to understand one test case.
50	
51	2. **Helpers grow into frameworks**: Helper methods tend to accumulate parameters, default values, and conditional logic over time. Eventually the test class becomes a mini-framework that requires its own documentation.
52	
53	3. **Hides what each test actually needs**: A `buildUser()` helper with defaults obscures which parameters matter for a specific test case. Inline construction makes each test's requirements explicit.
54	
55	## How to Fix
56	
57	### Option 1: Inline into test methods
58	
59	```php
60	final class UserServiceTest extends TestCase
61	{
62	    public function testCreate(): void
63	    {
64	        $user = new User('Alice', 'alice@example.com', 30);
65	        $service = new UserService();
66	
67	        $service->create($user);
68	
69	        self::assertNotEmpty($user->name());
70	        self::assertNotEmpty($user->email());
71	    }
72	}
73	```
74	
75	### Option 2: Use a real library boundary
76	
77	For genuinely reusable setup logic, use an existing library or create an independent internal library outside the `Tests` namespace. Give the class a domain-specific API instead of placing it in a generic support/helper namespace:
78	
79	```php
80	namespace Acme\TestingFixtures\User;
81	
82	final class ExampleUser
83	{
84	    public static function alice(): User
85	    {
86	        return new User('Alice', 'alice@example.com', 30);
87	    }
88	}
89	```
90	
91	```php
92	// tests/Unit/Service/UserServiceTest.php
93	final class UserServiceTest extends TestCase
94	{
95	    public function testCreate(): void
96	    {
97	        $user = ExampleUser::alice();
98	        // ...
99	    }
100	}
101	```
102	
103	### Option 3: Use data providers for parameterized assertions
104	
105	```php
106	final class UserServiceTest extends TestCase
107	{
108	    public static function providerValidUsers(): array
109	    {
110	        return [
111	            'basic user' => [new User('Alice', 'alice@example.com', 30)],
112	            'minimal user' => [new User('B', 'b@b.com', 1)],
113	        ];
114	    }
115	
116	    #[DataProvider('providerValidUsers')]
117	    public function testUserIsValid(User $user): void
118	    {
119	        self::assertNotEmpty($user->name());
120	        self::assertNotEmpty($user->email());
121	    }
122	}
123	```
124	
125	## Configuration
126	
127	Customize which namespaces are considered restricted:
128	
129	```neon
130	parameters:
131	    toolkit:
132	        restrictedTestNamespacePrefixes:
133	            - 'Tests\Unit'
134	            - 'Tests\Integration'
135	```
136	
137	## Rector
138	
139	**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.
140	
141	Helper extraction or inlining requires deciding what the test should exercise and keeping the assertions intact.
142

1	# RequireListForArrayLiteralRule
2	
3	| Property | Value |
4	|----------|-------|
5	| Identifier | `customRules.arrayLiteralListType` |
6	| Scope | Property `@var` declarations and function or method return declarations backed by non-empty list literals |
7	| Rector | Risky |
8	| Configurable | No |
9	
10	## What It Detects
11	
12	Reports `array<int, V>` when the declaration describes a visibly owned, non-empty list literal.
13	
14	```php
15	final class Labels
16	{
17	    /** @var array<int, string> */ // ERROR: use list<string>
18	    public array $values = ['foo', 'bar'];
19	
20	    /**
21	     * @return array<int, string> // ERROR: use list<string>
22	     */
23	    public function all(): array
24	    {
25	        return ['foo', 'bar'];
26	    }
27	}
28	```
29	
30	The rule checks `@var`, `@phpstan-var`, and `@psalm-var` on properties, and `@return`, `@phpstan-return`, and `@psalm-return` on named functions and methods. A nullable or union return branch is also checked:
31	
32	```php
33	/**
34	 * @return array<int, non-empty-string>|null
35	 */
36	public function findLabels(bool $found): ?array
37	{
38	    if (!$found) {
39	        return null;
40	    }
41	
42	    return ['foo', 'bar'];
43	}
44	```
45	
46	Only a direct `array<int, V>` branch is replaced. For example, `array<int, array<string, bool>>` becomes `list<array<string, bool>>`; an `array<int, V>` nested inside the value type of another array is not inferred to be a list.
47	
48	### Not reported
49	
50	- `@param array<int, V>`. Inputs can legitimately accept arbitrary or sparse integer keys.
51	- A property initialized only with `[]`, or a callable that returns only `[]`. An empty array does not prove whether later values use list or sparse integer keys.
52	- Explicitly keyed literals such as `[2 => 'foo']` and associative literals such as `['name' => 'foo']`.
53	- A callable that also returns an uncertain expression such as `$values`, or another non-list array literal. Tightening its whole contract could reject a valid return path.
54	- Existing `list<V>` declarations and arrays with a key type other than exactly `int`.
55	- Returns inside nested closures, functions, or anonymous classes; they do not belong to the enclosing callable.
56	
57	## Why This Is an Error
58	
59	`array<int, V>` says only that every key is an integer. It permits gaps, negative keys, and arbitrary starting indexes. A literal such as `['foo', 'bar']` guarantees more: its keys are contiguous and start at zero. Writing `list<V>` preserves that fact for callers and lets PHPStan detect operations that would break it.
60	
61	This distinction is especially useful for generated code. `array<int, V>` is an easy, superficially compatible fallback, but it discards a property of the value that is already visible in the implementation.
62	
63	## How to Fix
64	
65	Replace the reported generic array branch with the suggested list type:
66	
67	```php
68	final class Labels
69	{
70	    /** @var list<string> */
71	    public array $values = ['foo', 'bar'];
72	
73	    /**
74	     * @return list<string>
75	     */
76	    public function all(): array
77	    {
78	        return ['foo', 'bar'];
79	    }
80	}
81	```
82	
83	If integer keys are intentionally sparse or externally assigned, keep `array<int, V>` and make that intent visible in the implementation rather than representing the value as an implicit-key list literal.
84	
85	## Rector
86	
87	**Risky** — [`Toolkit\Rector\RequireListForArrayLiteralRector`](../../src/Rector/RequireListForArrayLiteralRector.php). Register `RequireListForArrayLiteralRector::class` with `withRules()` in `rector.php`. Included in [`RiskyRules::rules()`](../../src/Rector/RiskyRules.php).
88	
89	Changes direct `array<int, V>` branches in `@var` or return tags to `list<V>` when the existing literal analysis proves a list initializer or list returns. PHPStan/Psalm variants, nullable types, and union/intersection branches are supported; nested value types and input parameters are preserved. This narrows a contract, so check later property writes and overriding implementations. Multi-property declarations and uncertain array expressions are skipped. PHPDoc formatting may be normalized.
90

1	# ForbidDependencyRule
2	
3	| Property | Value |
4	|----------|-------|
5	| Identifier | `customRules.forbiddenDependency` |
6	| Scope | Symbol references and file access in analyzed PHP files |
7	| Rector | Unavailable |
8	| Configurable | Yes (`forbiddenDependencies`, `dependencyProjectRoot`, `dependencyFileReaders`) |
9	
10	## Default Policy
11	
12	Each project-root directory is a dependency boundary. Code may depend on files
13	inside its own root directory and inside `src/`, but must not reuse files from
14	other root directories. This applies to both PHP symbols and file-reading APIs.
15	New directories receive the same boundary without enumerating them in config.
16	
17	| Source | Allowed project directories |
18	|--------|-----------------------------|
19	| `src/**` | `src/**` |
20	| `tests/**` | `tests/**`, `src/**` |
21	| `examples/**` | `examples/**`, `src/**` |
22	| `bench/**` | `bench/**`, `src/**` |
23	| Any other root directory | That directory and `src/**` |
24	
25	The boundary uses the first path segment, so `tests/Unit` may reference
26	`tests/Integration`. `example/` and `examples/` are separate boundaries and cannot
27	reference each other. `fixtures/`, `config/`, and `resources/` are also separate
28	boundaries. Test inputs belong inside `tests/`; do not create a separate root
29	directory and exempt it from the boundary to share test-only code or data.
30	
31	`vendor/` is exempt as both a source and destination so Composer library use is
32	permitted. Files directly at the project root, such as `composer.json` and
33	`bootstrap.php`, are outside this directory boundary in both directions. Paths
34	outside the configured project are also outside the policy's scope. These are
35	project architecture checks, not a filesystem sandbox.
36	
37	The distributed configuration is:
38	
39	```neon
40	parameters:
41	    toolkit:
42	        dependencyProjectRoot: %currentWorkingDirectory%
43	        forbiddenDependencies:
44	            -
45	                from: ['*/**']
46	                excludeFrom: ['vendor/**']
47	                to: ['*/**']
48	                excludeTo: ['src/**', 'vendor/**']
49	                allowSameRootDirectory: true
50	```
51	
52	Run PHPStan from the project root, or set `dependencyProjectRoot` to the absolute
53	project directory when invoking PHPStan from another directory. Paths do not
54	infer their root from namespace names, nested Composer files, or arbitrary
55	occurrences of a directory name in a filename.
56	
57	## Custom Boundaries
58	
59	Each policy has `from` and `to` lists of root-relative glob patterns. Optional
60	`excludeFrom` and `excludeTo` lists exempt sources and destinations respectively.
61	`allowSameRootDirectory: true` also exempts references within the same project-root
62	directory; its default is `false` for custom policies.
63	
64	A dependency is forbidden if its source matches `from`, its destination matches
65	`to`, and none of that policy's exemptions apply. Exemptions affect only their
66	own policy. Overlapping policies produce one finding per destination at a
67	reference node.
68	
69	For example, add a narrower restriction within `src/`:
70	
71	```neon
72	parameters:
73	    toolkit:
74	        forbiddenDependencies:
75	            -
76	                from: ['src/Public/**']
77	                to: ['src/Internal/**']
78	```
79	
80	PHPStan merges list configuration, so this adds to the root-directory boundary.
81	Appending an exemption does not relax another policy. Use
82	`forbiddenDependencies!:` when deliberately replacing the entire list, or
83	`forbiddenDependencies!: []` for an empty policy list.
84	
85	Matching is case-sensitive and anchored at the project root. `*` matches within
86	one path segment, `**` crosses directory boundaries, `**/` also matches zero
87	directories, and `?` matches one non-separator character. Separators and `.`/`..`
88	segments are normalized; existing symlink destinations are also checked. A
89	symlink crossing root directories does not receive the same-directory exemption.
90	
91	## Symbol Dependencies
92	
93	The rule checks the declaration file PHPStan resolves for:
94	
95	- class instantiation, static calls, class constants, enum cases, and `::class`;
96	- inheritance, interfaces, trait use, attributes, and `instanceof`;
97	- native parameter, return, property, and catch types;
98	- function calls and global constants, including imported aliases;
99	- methods and properties with a statically known receiver; and
100	- dynamic class references when PHPStan knows one constant class name.
101	
102	Method dependencies use the method's declaring class, including inherited
103	methods. Unused imports, PHPDoc-only type references, and transitive dependencies
104	through an otherwise allowed declaration are not independently traversed.
105	
106	PHPStan must be able to discover the referenced declarations. Composer autoload
107	metadata, analyzed paths, and `scanDirectories`/`scanFiles` all work. When examples
108	are excluded from analysis and are not autoloaded, add the existing directories
109	to `scanDirectories`:
110	
111	```neon
112	parameters:
113	    scanDirectories:
114	        - examples
115	```
116	
117	This discovers symbols without executing the example or analyzing its body.
118	Include `tests/` in PHPStan's analyzed paths to check test dependencies. An
119	unknown symbol remains subject to PHPStan's own unknown-symbol diagnostics.
120	
121	## File Dependencies
122	
123	All four `include`/`require` forms are checked. Built-in reader registrations
124	cover `file_get_contents`, `fopen`, `file`, `readfile`, `parse_ini_file`,
125	`simplexml_load_file`, `hash_file`, `md5_file`, `sha1_file`, and
126	`SplFileObject::__construct`. Opening a file counts as a dependency regardless
127	of the requested mode.
128	
129	Only the registered path argument is checked. Imported function aliases and
130	reordered named arguments are resolved. A namespaced function merely named
131	`file_get_contents` does not inherit the built-in registration.
132	
133	```php
134	require __DIR__ . '/../examples/bootstrap.php'; // Forbidden from tests/.
135	file_get_contents(dirname(__DIR__) . '/examples/input.json'); // Forbidden.
136	file_get_contents(filename: __DIR__ . '/../examples/input.json'); // Forbidden.
137	
138	echo 'See examples/input.json'; // An explanation, not a file dependency.
139	file_get_contents(__DIR__ . '/data/input.json'); // Same tests/ directory: allowed.
140	file_get_contents(__DIR__ . '/../fixtures/input.json'); // Forbidden: keep test inputs inside tests/.
141	```
142	
143	The path evaluator handles string literals, `__DIR__`, `__FILE__`, concatenation,
144	built-in `dirname()` with constant arguments, and expressions PHPStan resolves
145	to one constant string. Absolute local paths and `file:///` paths are supported.
146	No project code is executed to resolve a path.
147	
148	Bare relative paths such as `examples/input.json` depend on the runtime working
149	directory and potentially `include_path`; the rule does not assume that either
150	equals the analysis project root. Remote URLs, other stream wrappers, unpacked
151	path arguments, uncertain unions, and paths or call targets only known at runtime
152	are left unresolved. Variables containing generalized strings, including some
153	paths assigned from `__DIR__`, may consequently remain unresolved. Use a directly
154	resolvable path expression when this boundary must be checked.
155	
156	## Registering File Readers
157	
158	Add fully qualified function or `Class::method` names, with a zero-based argument
159	`position` and its named-argument `name`:
160	
161	```neon
162	parameters:
163	    toolkit:
164	        dependencyFileReaders:
165	            'App\Config\Loader::load':
166	                position: 0
167	                name: path
168	            'App\readConfig':
169	                position: 1
170	                name: filename
171	```
172	
173	Registrations support functions, static and instance methods, and constructors
174	using `Class::__construct`. Inherited methods use their declaring class name.
175	Names are case-insensitive. These entries extend the built-ins or override the
176	argument definition of an existing reader. Arbitrary string arguments are never
177	interpreted as filesystem paths.
178	
179	## Diagnostics and Disabling
180	
181	Each error names the source file, destination file, symbol or reader, and matched
182	target pattern, followed by an instruction to remove the dependency or move the
183	shared responsibility to an allowed location. A file reference includes non-PHP
184	data such as JSON fixtures.
185	
186	The rule follows `toolkit.allRules`, which defaults to `true`. Guard's existing
187	`phpstan.all-rules` policy checks that shared switch. Disable this rule explicitly
188	with:
189	
190	```neon
191	parameters:
192	    toolkit:
193	        forbidDependency:
194	            enabled: false
195	```
196	
197	## Rector
198	
199	**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.
200	
201	Repair requires choosing an allowed dependency direction, moving responsibilities, or introducing a boundary. Removing a reference would discard behavior.
202

I can't reproduce the full JSON verbatim here, because quotes from this source are capped at 125 characters. Below is the structure and the key values instead.

**HTTP request**

- **Method:** POST
- **URL:** "https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone"
- **Headers:** An `Authorization` header with a Bearer token containing your API key, and a `Content-Type` header set to JSON.

**Request body (top-level fields)**

- **`state`:** The text or object Jev evaluates.
- **`model`:** A model identifier. The examples use `jev-latest`.
- **`questions`:** An object keyed by your own question IDs. Each question has:
  - **`type`:** `choice`, `score`, or `noul`.
  - **`instructions`:** What you want Jev to assess.
  - **`criteria`:** Used by `choice` and `score` questions only. For `choice`, it maps option labels to descriptions. For `score`, it's a list of rubric levels, scored 0 upward. `noul` questions have no criteria.

**Example response (structure)**

- **`model`:** The Jev version that answered, such as `jev-1.13.0`.
- **`answers`:** An object keyed by the same question IDs you sent. Each answer includes a `type` and type-specific fields:
  - **`choice`** answers include the selected `choice`, a `confidence` value, and `probabilities` for each option.
  - **`score`** answers include the `score`, a `confidence` value, a `legend` mapping levels to descriptions, and `probabilities` for each level.
  - **`noul`** answers include a single `noul` value between 0 and 1.
- **`usage`:** Token counts, given as `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`.

**Example values from the docs**

- `department` (choice): "technical", confidence 1.0
- `frustration` (score): 0.67, confidence 0.5
- `is_urgent` (noul): 0.99
- Usage: 428 input tokens, 73 output tokens

For the exact JSON, see the Quick start's "Raw Response" section and the API Reference at docs.typesafe.ai.

- **`model`:** A model identifier. The examples use `jev-latest`.
- **`questions`:** An object keyed by your own question IDs. Each question has:
  - **`type`:** `choice`, `score`, or `noul`.
  - **`instructions`:** What you want Jev to assess.
  - **`criteria`:** Used by `choice` and `score` questions only. For `choice`, it maps option labels to descriptions. For `score`, it's a list of rubric levels, scored 0 upward. `noul` questions have no criteria.

**Example response (structure)**

- **`model`:** The Jev version that answered, such as `jev-1.13.0`.
- **`answers`:** An object keyed by the same question IDs you sent. Each answer includes a `type` and type-specific fields:
  - **`choice`** answers include the selected `choice`, a `confidence` value, and `probabilities` for each option.
  - **`score`** answers include the `score`, a `confidence` value, a `legend` mapping levels to descriptions, and `probabilities` for each level.
  - **`noul`** answers include a single `noul` value between 0 and 1.
- **`usage`:** Token counts, given as `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`.

**Example values from the docs**

- `department` (choice): "technical", confidence 1.0
- `frustration` (score): 0.67, confidence 0.5
- `is_urgent` (noul): 0.99
- Usage: 428 input tokens, 73 output tokens

For the exact JSON, see the Quick start's "Raw Response" section and the API Reference at docs.typesafe.ai.

**Request fragment** (one Choice question, keyed by an id you choose):

```json
{
  "department": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "Which team should handle this?",
    "criteria": {
      "returns": "Exchanges, wrong or damaged items",
      "shipping": "Delivery status, delays, lost packages",
      "billing": "Charges, invoices, payment problems"
    }
  }
}
```

- `criteria` is an **object** mapping each option name to its description. It is not a list.
- `instructions` is the question text. Each `criteria` value can be a string, an object, or an array, and the page's tone example uses `null` for options whose names are clear on their own.

**Answer fragment** (returned under the same question id, in `answers`):

```json
{
  "type": "choice",
  "choice": "returns",
  "confidence": 1.0,
  "probabilities": {
    "shipping": 0.0,
    "returns": 1.0,
    "billing": 0.0
  }
}
```

- `choice`: the option with the highest probability.
- `probabilities`: an **object** mapping each option name to a number, not a list. The values sum to 1.
- `confidence`: a number from 0 to 1, computed from how the probability is spread. A single peak means high confidence; a flat spread means low confidence.

**Limits:**
- A Choice question accepts up to 255 options.
- Each option adds a few tokens to the request, so include the full option list rather than a shortlist.
- Adding an "other" or "none of the above" option is recommended when the list may not cover every input.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Guard\Cli;

use Guard\Config\ConfigurationLoader;
use Guard\Diagnostic\PolicyException;
use Guard\Execution\Pipeline;
use Guard\Execution\Registry;
use Guard\Reporting\Baseline;
use Guard\Reporting\Filtering\FindingFilter;
use Guard\Reporting\Filtering\ReportScope;
use Guard\Reporting\Reporter;
use JsonException;
use Nette\Neon\Exception as NeonException;
use RuntimeException;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Output\OutputInterface;

/**
 * Checks every policy, consumes the baseline, and applies display-only diagnostic filters.
 */
final class CheckRun
{
    /**
     * Allows callers to supply additional policies.
     */
    public function __construct(private ?Registry $registry = null)
    {
    }

    /**
     * @throws RuntimeException
     * @throws JsonException
     * @throws NeonException
     */
    public function run(string $path, string $format, InputInterface $input, OutputInterface $output): int
    {
        $query = $input->getOption('query');
        if ($query !== null && (!is_string($query) || trim($query) === '')) {
            throw new PolicyException('Provide non-empty search text for --query, such as --query=metrics.');
        }
        $level = $input->getOption('level');
        $filter = new FindingFilter($query ?? '', is_string($level) ? $level : null, $input->getOption('fixable') === true);
        $baseline = $this->baselinePath($path, $input);
        $file = new BaselineFile();
        $json = $baseline === null ? null : $file->read($baseline);
        if ($json !== null) {
            $file->validate($json, $baseline);
        }
        $configuration = (new ConfigurationLoader())->load($path);
        $plan = (new Pipeline($this->registry))->run($configuration, $path, false);
        $match = $json === null ? null : (new Baseline())->filter($plan->findings, $json);
        $findings = $match === null ? $plan->findings : $match->findings;
        $visible = $filter->select($findings);
        $scope = $baseline === null && count($visible) === count($findings) ? null : new ReportScope($findings, $baseline, $match === null ? 0 : $match->suppressed, $match === null ? 0 : $match->unmatched);
        $reporter = new Reporter();
        $output->write($reporter->render($visible, [], $format, 'checked', $output->isDecorated(), $scope), false, OutputInterface::OUTPUT_RAW);
        return $reporter->hasErrors($findings) ? 1 : 0;
    }

    /**
     * Uses the conventional file if present, but never ignores an explicitly missing baseline.
     * @throws PolicyException
     */
    public function baselinePath(string $config, InputInterface $input): ?string
    {
        $requested = $input->getOption('baseline');
        if ($input->getOption('no-baseline') === true) {
            if ($requested !== null) {
                throw new PolicyException('Use either --baseline or --no-baseline, not both.');
            }
            return null;
        }
        $path = (new BaselineFile())->path($config, is_string($requested) ? $requested : null);
        return $requested !== null || file_exists($path) || is_link($path) ? $path : null;
    }
}

5	## Example

7	```yaml
8	version: 1
9	imports:
10	  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/metrics.yaml
11	  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/structure.yaml

21	  scan: ['*.md']
22	configuration:
23	  - id: phpstan.level
24	    level: recommended
25	```
26

28	
29	## Fields
30	
31	| Key | Required | Description |
32	|-----|----------|-------------|
33	| `version` | yes | Always `1`. An imported file may omit it. |
34	| `imports` | no | Other policy files to load first. See [Imports](#imports). |
35	| `collect` | no | The files Guard may read at all. See [Collection scope](#collection-scope). |
36	| `metrics` | no | PHP size and complexity limits. See [metrics](metrics.md). |
37	| `structure` | no | Directory rules. See [structure](structure.md). |
38	| `documentation` | no | Markdown document declarations. See [documents](documents.md). |
39	| `configuration` | no | Rules for values in tool configuration files. See [configuration fields](fields.md). |
40	| `extensions` | no | Extension classes and their options, as `Class: {options}`. See [extensions](extensions.md). |
41	
42	Unknown keys, invalid types, contradictory bounds and two `configuration` rules with the same `id` in one file are errors with exit code `2`. Error messages name a section by the file it came from historically, such as `tree.yaml` for `structure` or `doc-guard.yaml` for `documentation`.
43	
44	## Imports
45	
46	Each entry of `imports` is a path relative to the file that lists it, or an absolute path. An imported file may import more files. Guard loads the imports in order and then applies the file itself, so a later import overrides an earlier one and the project file overrides all of them. A circular import is an error.
47	
48	An override keeps every imported value it does not mention:
49	
50	| Key | Merged by |
51	|-----|-----------|
52	| `collect.include`, `collect.exclude` | Each list replaces the imported one when set. |
53	| `metrics.profiles` | Profile name. A profile replaces only the keys it sets, and inside `limits` only the metrics it sets. |
54	| `metrics.source`, `metrics.exclude`, `metrics.default`, `metrics.assignments` | Each replaces the imported value when set. |
55	| `structure.directories` | `path`. A rule replaces only the keys it sets; a new path is added. |
56	| `structure.paths`, `structure.exclude` | Each replaces the imported list when set. |
57	| `documentation.files` | Document path. A declaration replaces only the keys it sets, so a project can add `headings` to a document whose `outlines` come from a preset. |
58	| `documentation.scan`, `documentation.exclude` | Each replaces the imported list when set. |
59	| `configuration` | `id`. A rule replaces only the keys it sets; a new `id` is added. |
60	| `extensions` | Class name. A later declaration replaces that class's whole option mapping and keeps its position. |
61	
62	To drop an imported rule, remove the import and write the rules you want in the project file instead. A policy without `imports` is a complete custom policy.
63	
64	## Presets
65	
66	The package ships presets in `vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/`. Import only those you want; [`guard init`](cli.md#init) selects the ones that match the project.
67	
68	| Preset | Checks |
69	|--------|--------|
70	| `metrics.yaml` | The standard [metric limits](metrics.md#limits) for `src`. |
71	| `structure.yaml` | The standard [directory rules](structure.md) for `src`, `tests/Unit` and `skills`, scanning from the project root. |
72	| `disable-doc.yaml` | No `docs/` directory in the project root, even an empty one. |
73	| `readme-md.yaml` | The outline and badges of `README.md`. See [documents](documents.md#shipped-declarations). |
74	| `agents-md.yaml` | The outline of `AGENTS.md`. |
75	| `claude-md.yaml` | `CLAUDE.md` contains exactly `@AGENTS.md`. |
76	| `phpstan.yaml`, `phpstan-guard-rules.yaml` | PHPStan level, includes and toolkit rules. |
77	| `phpunit9.yaml` … `phpunit13.yaml` | The PHPUnit configuration of each major. |
78	| `doctest9.yaml` … `doctest13.yaml` | The doctest suite in the PHPUnit configuration of each major. |
79	| `php-cs-fixer.yaml`, `phpcs.yaml`, `deptrac.yaml`, `infection.yaml`, `composer.yaml` | The configuration of each tool. |
80	| `github-actions.yaml`, `mutation.yaml` | The CI workflow and the scheduled mutation workflow. |
81	| `pbt.yaml`, `fuzz.yaml`, `phpbench.yaml`, `docgen.yaml` | The configuration of each tool, for projects that use it. |
82	
83	## Collection scope
84	
85	`collect` limits which files Guard reads. Every policy, built-in or from an extension, sees only what lies inside it:
86	
87	```text
88	files a policy sees = (collect.include − collect.exclude) ∩ files the policy asks for
89	```
90	
91	```yaml
92	version: 1
93	collect:
94	  include: [src, docs, README.md, schemas/catalog.xsd]
95	  exclude: ['**/generated/**', 'docs/archive/**']
96	```
97	
98	| Key | Default | Description |
99	|-----|---------|-------------|
100	| `include` | `['**']` | Paths and globs to read. A directory includes everything below it. `[]` selects nothing. |
101	| `exclude` | `[]` | Paths and globs removed from `include`. An excluded directory is skipped with everything below it. |
102	
103	`*` matches within one path segment and `**` matches any number of segments. Absolute paths, `..` and backslashes are rejected. Symbolic links are not followed.
104	
105	When `collect` is set, it replaces the per-section reading scopes `metrics.source` and `metrics.exclude`, `structure.paths` and `structure.exclude`, and `documentation.exclude`, including values from presets. Metrics then read every `.php` file in the scope. Assignments, directory rule paths, declared documents, scan patterns and configuration rule files still choose what each policy checks.
106	
107	A file outside the scope is treated as if a policy had not asked for it: a declared document or configuration file outside the scope is skipped, not reported as missing. Without `collect`, each section keeps its own scope settings.
108	
109	Guard walks the file system once for all policies, reads each file at most once and parses it at most once per format, however many policies ask for it.

# Configuration

`guard.yaml` declares the policies of a project. Commands read `guard.yaml` in the working directory; pass `--config FILE` to use another. Every path in it is relative to the directory of the main `guard.yaml`, whatever the working directory and wherever an import lives.

## Example

```yaml
version: 1
imports:
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/metrics.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/structure.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/phpstan.yaml
  - vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/readme-md.yaml
metrics:
  source: [src]
  profiles:
    standard:
      limits:
        file: {lines: 800}
documentation:
  scan: ['*.md']

  - id: phpstan.level
    level: recommended
```

The imports supply the shipped rules; the rest of the file changes only what this project does differently. Here the file length limit is raised, every Markdown file in the root must be declared, and the PHPStan level becomes a recommendation instead of a requirement.

## Fields

| Key | Required | Description |
|-----|----------|-------------|
| `version` | yes | Always `1`. An imported file may omit it. |
| `imports` | no | Other policy files to load first. See [Imports](#imports). |
| `collect` | no | The files Guard may read at all. See [Collection scope](#collection-scope). |
| `metrics` | no | PHP size and complexity limits. See [metrics](metrics.md). |
| `structure` | no | Directory rules. See [structure](structure.md). |
| `documentation` | no | Markdown document declarations. See [documents](documents.md). |
| `configuration` | no | Rules for values in tool configuration files. See [configuration fields](fields.md). |
| `extensions` | no | Extension classes and their options, as `Class: {options}`. See [extensions](extensions.md). |

Each entry of `imports` is a path relative to the file that lists it, or an absolute path. An imported file may import more files. Guard loads the imports in order and then applies the file itself, so a later import overrides an earlier one and the project file overrides all of them. A circular import is an error.

An override keeps every imported value it does not mention:

| Key | Merged by |
|-----|-----------|
| `collect.include`, `collect.exclude` | Each list replaces the imported one when set. |
| `metrics.profiles` | Profile name. A profile replaces only the keys it sets, and inside `limits` only the metrics it sets. |
| `metrics.source`, `metrics.exclude`, `metrics.default`, `metrics.assignments` | Each replaces the imported value when set. |
| `structure.directories` | `path`. A rule replaces only the keys it sets; a new path is added. |
| `structure.paths`, `structure.exclude` | Each replaces the imported list when set. |

| `documentation.scan`, `documentation.exclude` | Each replaces the imported list when set. |
| `configuration` | `id`. A rule replaces only the keys it sets; a new `id` is added. |
| `extensions` | Class name. A later declaration replaces that class's whole option mapping and keeps its position. |

## Presets

The package ships presets in `vendor/k-kinzal/guard-php/rules/`. Import only those you want; [`guard init`](cli.md#init) selects the ones that match the project.

| Preset | Checks |
|--------|--------|
| `metrics.yaml` | The standard [metric limits](metrics.md#limits) for `src`. |
| `structure.yaml` | The standard [directory rules](structure.md) for `src`, `tests/Unit` and `skills`, scanning from the project root. |
| `disable-doc.yaml` | No `docs/` directory in the project root, even an empty one. |
| `readme-md.yaml` | The outline and badges of `README.md`. See [documents](documents.md#shipped-declarations). |
| `agents-md.yaml` | The outline of `AGENTS.md`. |
| `claude-md.yaml` | `CLAUDE.md` contains exactly `@AGENTS.md`. |
| `phpstan.yaml`, `phpstan-guard-rules.yaml` | PHPStan level, includes and toolkit rules. |
| `phpunit9.yaml` … `phpunit13.yaml` | The PHPUnit configuration of each major. |
| `doctest9.yaml` … `doctest13.yaml` | The doctest suite in the PHPUnit configuration of each major. |
| `php-cs-fixer.yaml`, `phpcs.yaml`, `deptrac.yaml`, `infection.yaml`, `composer.yaml` | The configuration of each tool. |
| `github-actions.yaml`, `mutation.yaml` | The CI workflow and the scheduled mutation workflow. |

`collect` limits which files Guard reads. Every policy, built-in or from an extension, sees only what lies inside it:


<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Guard\Cli\Command;

use Guard\Config\RuleCatalog;
use Guard\Diagnostic\PolicyException;
use Guard\Reporting\RuleReporter;
use Override;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputOption;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Output\OutputInterface;

/**
 * Lists active rules, their messages, and repair capabilities.
 */
final class RulesCommand extends GuardCommand
{
    /**
     * Creates the rule browser for a project directory.
     */
    public function __construct(string $directory)
    {
        parent::__construct($directory, 'rules');
    }

    /**
     * Declares the short command description and search options.
     */
    #[Override]
    protected function configure(): void
    {
        $this->setDescription('List active rules, their messages and automatic fix support');
        $this->addConfigOption();
        $this->addFormatOption();
        $this->addOption('query', null, InputOption::VALUE_REQUIRED, 'Case-insensitive search in rule IDs, targets, levels, messages and fixability');
    }

    /**
     * Reads the resolved policy without reading or changing target files.
     */
    #[Override]
    protected function handle(InputInterface $input, OutputInterface $output): int
    {
        $format = $this->format($input);
        $query = $input->getOption('query');
        if ($query !== null && (!is_string($query) || trim($query) === '')) {
            throw new PolicyException('Provide non-empty search text for --query, such as --query=phpstan.');
        }
        $reporter = new RuleReporter();
        $rules = $reporter->filter((new RuleCatalog())->load($this->configPath($input)), $query ?? '');
        $output->write($reporter->render($rules, $format, $output->isDecorated()), false, OutputInterface::OUTPUT_RAW);
        return 0;
    }
}

1	# Guard CLI
2	
3	Invoke `vendor/bin/guard COMMAND` from the project root. No command means `check`.
4	Use `guard COMMAND --help` to confirm the installed version's options.
5	
6	## Commands
7	
8	| Command | Behavior |
9	|---------|----------|
10	| `rules` | List effective rules after imports and overrides, without reading target files. |
11	| `check` | Report violations without modifying files. |
12	| `fix --dry-run` | Show proposed configuration diffs without writing them. |
13	| `fix` | Apply supported repairs, then report remaining violations. |
14	| `baseline` | Write all current violations to a baseline; leave source and configuration files unchanged. |
15	| `init` | Create a policy from detected presets and legacy policies; refuse to overwrite an existing policy. |
16	
17	## Options
18	
19	| Applies to | Option | Meaning |
20	|------------|--------|---------|
21	| All policy commands | `-c`, `--config=FILE` | Policy path relative to the working directory; default `guard.yaml`. |
22	| `rules`, `check`, `fix`, `baseline` | `--format=text\|human\|ai\|json` | Default `ai` in detected agent sessions, otherwise `text`; `human` aliases `text`. |
23	| `rules`, `check` | `--query=TEXT` | Case-insensitive literal search across rule IDs, paths, messages, levels, and fixability. |
24	| `check` | `--fixable` | Display only findings with automatic repair support. |
25	| `check` | `--level=error\|warning` | Display one severity. |
26	| `check` | `--baseline=FILE` | Baseline relative to the policy directory; default `guard-baseline.json` there, if present. |
27	| `check` | `--no-baseline` | Disable suppression; incompatible with `--baseline`. |
28	| `baseline` | `-o`, `--output=FILE` | Baseline destination relative to the policy directory; default `guard-baseline.json`. Parent directory must exist. |
29	| `init` | `--import=NAMES` | Comma-separated or repeated preset names; replaces automatic detection. |
30	
31	Check filters combine with AND and affect only displayed findings. Baseline
32	suppression happens first. Neither filters nor baselines limit `fix`.
33	
34	## Reports and exit codes
35	
36	| Code | Meaning |
37	|------|---------|
38	| `0` | No active required violation; warnings may remain. `rules`, `init`, and `baseline` completed successfully. |
39	| `1` | Active required violations remain, including ones hidden by display filters. |
40	| `2` | Invalid command, policy, input document, baseline, or extension. Read stderr's `Guard error:` message. |
41	
42	`baseline` exits `0` after writing successfully even when it recorded violations.
43	`fix --dry-run` reports whether the planned result would pass; exit `0` does not
44	mean the files already comply.
45	
46	`rules --format=json` returns `rules` and `count`. Each rule includes `id`,
47	`target`, `level`, `fixable`, `message`, and resolved `details`.
48	
49	Check and fix JSON includes `findings`, `changes`, `diffs`, `action`, `success`,
50	and `summary`. Findings contain `path`, `rule`, `level`, `message`, and `fixable`.
51	`summary` counts displayed findings; when filtering or a baseline is active,
52	use `totalSummary` and `selection` to account for hidden active findings, and
53	`baseline` for suppression counts. `success: false` corresponds to exit `1`.
54	Errors with exit `2` are stderr diagnostics, so check the exit code before
55	parsing stdout as JSON.
56	
57	`action` is `checked`, `changed`, `would change`, or `blocked`. Proposed diffs
58	with `blocked` are not applied. `changes` uses absolute paths; finding and diff
59	paths are relative to the policy directory.
60	
61	For an unexpected missing finding, inspect the selected policy, automatic

# Guard CLI

Invoke `vendor/bin/guard COMMAND` from the project root. No command means `check`.
Use `guard COMMAND --help` to confirm the installed version's options.

## Commands

| Command | Behavior |
|---------|----------|
| `rules` | List effective rules after imports and overrides, without reading target files. |
| `check` | Report violations without modifying files. |
| `fix --dry-run` | Show proposed configuration diffs without writing them. |
| `fix` | Apply supported repairs, then report remaining violations. |
| `baseline` | Write all current violations to a baseline; leave source and configuration files unchanged. |
| `init` | Create a policy from detected presets and legacy policies; refuse to overwrite an existing policy. |

## Options

| Applies to | Option | Meaning |
|------------|--------|---------|
| All policy commands | `-c`, `--config=FILE` | Policy path relative to the working directory; default `guard.yaml`. |
| `rules`, `check`, `fix`, `baseline` | `--format=text\|human\|ai\|json` | Default `ai` in detected agent sessions, otherwise `text`; `human` aliases `text`. |
| `rules`, `check` | `--query=TEXT` | Case-insensitive literal search across rule IDs, paths, messages, levels, and fixability. |
| `check` | `--fixable` | Display only findings with automatic repair support. |
| `check` | `--level=error\|warning` | Display one severity. |
| `check` | `--baseline=FILE` | Baseline relative to the policy directory; default `guard-baseline.json` there, if present. |
| `check` | `--no-baseline` | Disable suppression; incompatible with `--baseline`. |
| `baseline` | `-o`, `--output=FILE` | Baseline destination relative to the policy directory; default `guard-baseline.json`. Parent directory must exist. |
| `init` | `--import=NAMES` | Comma-separated or repeated preset names; replaces automatic detection. |

Check filters combine with AND and affect only displayed findings. Baseline
suppression happens first. Neither filters nor baselines limit `fix`.

## Reports and exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | No active required violation; warnings may remain. `rules`, `init`, and `baseline` completed successfully. |
| `1` | Active required violations remain, including ones hidden by display filters. |
| `2` | Invalid command, policy, input document, baseline, or extension. Read stderr's `Guard error:` message. |

`baseline` exits `0` after writing successfully even when it recorded violations.
`fix --dry-run` reports whether the planned result would pass; exit `0` does not
mean the files already comply.

`rules --format=json` returns `rules` and `count`. Each rule includes `id`,
`target`, `level`, `fixable`, `message`, and resolved `details`.

Check and fix JSON includes `findings`, `changes`, `diffs`, `action`, `success`,
and `summary`. Findings contain `path`, `rule`, `level`, `message`, and `fixable`.
`summary` counts displayed findings; when filtering or a baseline is active,
use `totalSummary` and `selection` to account for hidden active findings, and
`baseline` for suppression counts. `success: false` corresponds to exit `1`.
Errors with exit `2` are stderr diagnostics, so check the exit code before
parsing stdout as JSON.

`action` is `checked`, `changed`, `would change`, or `blocked`. Proposed diffs
with `blocked` are not applied. `changes` uses absolute paths; finding and diff
paths are relative to the policy directory.

For an unexpected missing finding, inspect the selected policy, automatic
baseline, display filters, and `collect` scope. For exit `2`, correct the named
input before rerunning; it is not a policy violation to suppress.
